clusters.title: Adopt accessibility APIs
clusters.rule: Adopt accessibility APIs like VoiceOver, Switch Control, and Voice Control for assistive technology support.

clusters.title: Design keyboard-first navigation
clusters.rule: Design keyboard-first navigation and test that pages read logically to screen reader users.

clusters.title: Design snippets readable without speech
clusters.rule: Design snippets to be understood visually without relying on spoken dialog for accessibility.

clusters.title: Enable voice control for coding
clusters.rule: Enable voice control to write code by understanding Swift syntax, spacing, operators, and camel-casing.

clusters.title: Provide larger click targets for difficult actions
clusters.rule: Make frequently used or hard-to-reverse controls larger than 44×44 pixels to prevent mistakes.

clusters.title: Keep focus on triggering element
clusters.rule: Keep focus on the triggering element while the tooltip displays to preserve context.

clusters.title: Show visual focus indicator in trees
clusters.rule: Show a visual keyboard indicator when an item receives focus in a tree view.

clusters.title: Use heading hierarchy for skipping
clusters.rule: Use heading hierarchy to allow screen reader users to skip to main content directly.

clusters.title: Structure content logically
clusters.rule: Structure content logically so people with cognitive disabilities can find and prioritize information.

clusters.title: Provide larger menu targets
clusters.rule: Provide larger click targets in menus for users with fine motor difficulties.

clusters.title: Describe function not appearance
clusters.rule: Describe function, not appearance, for images used as buttons or links in alt text.

clusters.title: Replicate readable text in alt text
clusters.rule: Replicate text content exactly in alt text for images containing readable text.

clusters.title: Convey image meaning in alt text
clusters.rule: Convey image meaning, not literal appearance, in alt text for informative images.

clusters.title: Omit captions only when redundant
clusters.rule: Omit captions only when video merely restates information already presented as text on the page.

clusters.title: Use pauses for audio description
clusters.rule: Use pauses in dialogue to insert audio descriptions of actions, characters, scene changes, and on-screen text.

clusters.title: Avoid audio description if already audible
clusters.rule: Avoid requiring audio description if all video information is already audibly conveyed in the main soundtrack.

clusters.title: Place label text at control start
clusters.rule: Place label text at the start of a control's programmatic name for screen reader users.

clusters.title: Use text instead of text images
clusters.rule: Use text instead of images of text so users can adjust font size, color, and spacing.

clusters.title: Use images of text only when essential
clusters.rule: Only use images for text when the presentation is essential, such as logos or type samples.

clusters.title: Reduce background audio volume
clusters.rule: Ensure background audio in speech content is at least 20 decibels lower than foreground speech, or allow disabling.

findings.finding: Background sound at 20 dB is approximately four times quieter than foreground speech.

clusters.title: Advise users how to escape focus traps
clusters.rule: Advise users how to escape focus traps if exit requires non-standard methods beyond arrow, Tab, or Esc.

clusters.title: Avoid single-character shortcuts
clusters.rule: Avoid single-character keyboard shortcuts, especially for speech input users risking accidental triggers.

clusters.title: Offer text input as drag alternative
clusters.rule: Offer text input as an alternative to dragging for precise control and accessibility.

clusters.title: Screen readers load correct pronunciation
clusters.rule: Screen readers load correct pronunciation rules when page language is specified; mark language changes.

clusters.title: Trap focus inside modals
clusters.rule: Trap keyboard focus inside a modal until dismissed; Tab and Shift-Tab must not move focus outside.

clusters.title: Group related UI elements
clusters.rule: Group related UI elements together to reduce navigation time for screen reader users.

clusters.title: Label icon-only buttons with text
clusters.rule: Add text labels or alternatives for icon-only buttons so all users understand their function.

clusters.title: Provide non-visual feedback alternatives
clusters.rule: Provide non-visual alternatives like sound, vibration, or text for color-only microinteraction feedback.

clusters.title: Detect animated events for screen readers
clusters.rule: Ensure screen readers detect animated events, state changes, and overlays to prevent missing information.

clusters.title: Keep motion moderate
clusters.rule: Keep motion design moderate to prevent dizziness and disorientation in users with vestibular disorders.

clusters.title: Position notifications for magnified users
clusters.rule: Position animated notifications on-screen for low-vision users with screen magnification.

clusters.title: Provide UI detection for screen readers
clusters.rule: Provide automated UI detection to assist screen reader users accessing poorly labeled apps.

findings.finding: 71.3% mean average precision on 5,002 test screenshots across 13 UI element types

clusters.title: Communicate toggle states visually
clusters.rule: Recognize UI selection states visually using tint color and detection type to communicate toggles and checkboxes.

findings.finding: 90.5% recall for tab button selection state, 73.6% for segmented controls

clusters.title: Use left-aligned headings on confirmation
clusters.rule: Use left-aligned heading text on confirmation pages for accessibility with screen readers.

clusters.title: Never auto-submit on selection
clusters.rule: Never auto-submit forms when users select an option from interactive controls.

clusters.title: Offer open file formats
clusters.rule: Offer open file formats like ODT instead of proprietary types like XLS so users can open files with any software.

clusters.title: Use clear, descriptive link text
clusters.rule: Make link text clear and descriptive; avoid generic text like 'click here'.

clusters.title: Do not set inflexible deadlines
clusters.rule: Do not set inflexible deadlines; account for users who cannot respond quickly due to circumstances.

clusters.title: Test gestures with low muscle tone users
clusters.rule: Test gesture-based interactions with users who have low muscle tone to ensure minimal energy requirement.

clusters.title: Vary feedback frequency for accessibility
clusters.rule: Vary feedback frequency based on accessibility mode: increase repetition when VoiceOver is on.

clusters.title: Provide pronunciation hints for voice
clusters.rule: Provide pronunciation hints for voice options to avoid verbosity, reading only differentiating details aloud.

clusters.title: Use semantic markup for structure
clusters.rule: Use semantic markup for headings, lists, and tables to convey meaning and structure.

clusters.title: Use ARIA roles for semantic meaning
clusters.rule: Use WAI-ARIA roles to provide additional semantic meaning beyond semantic HTML elements.

clusters.title: Match code order to reading order
clusters.rule: Match code order to the logical reading order; remove CSS and verify content order makes sense.

clusters.title: Ensure comparable experience quality
clusters.rule: Ensure comparable experience quality and efficiency for all users regardless of ability or approach.

clusters.title: Never suppress browser settings
clusters.rule: Never suppress standard browser settings like zoom, orientation, font size, or contrast.

clusters.title: Offer customizable media alternatives
clusters.rule: Offer customizable alternatives like color-coded, repositionable captions for video to enhance experience.

clusters.title: Use live regions for proactive notification
clusters.rule: Use live regions to notify screen reader users proactively without requiring explicit user action.

clusters.title: Design with disability safeguards
clusters.rule: Recognize users with disabilities are more likely to make mistakes; require safeguards and extra confirmation.

clusters.title: Use shift triple-press for activation
clusters.rule: Use shift key triple-press as accessible discreet activation method for keyboard-only users.

clusters.title: Confirm destructive actions
clusters.rule: Confirm destructive actions with a second step; do not rely on color alone for warning.

clusters.title: Use visually hidden text for clarity
clusters.rule: Use visually hidden text to clarify what each change link modifies for screen reader users.

clusters.title: Avoid wrapping cards in anchor tags
clusters.rule: Avoid wrapping entire clickable cards in anchor tags due to poor screen reader experience.

clusters.title: Ensure contrast in translucent components
clusters.rule: Ensure text and graphical elements in translucent components meet WCAG contrast requirements.

clusters.title: Accessibility benefits all users
clusters.rule: Design for accessibility needs; accessible solutions benefit all users by making products easier to use.

clusters.title: Focus alt text on purpose not appearance
clusters.rule: Screen-reader users prioritize task information; focus alt text on purpose and function, not appearance.

clusters.title: Accommodate age-related vision changes
clusters.rule: Accommodate visual impairments including nearsightedness, farsightedness, astigmatism, presbyopia, and cataracts.

clusters.title: Accommodate hearing loss needs
clusters.rule: Accommodate hearing loss ranging from mild to profound; 5%+ of the world's population needs this support.

findings.finding: 5% of world population

clusters.title: Design for motor impairments
clusters.rule: Design for motor impairments common in aging: reduced range of motion, coordination loss, stroke, Parkinson's.

clusters.title: Use clear instructions for cognitive changes
clusters.rule: Use clear instructions and short, realistic tasks to accommodate cognitive changes affecting memory and attention.

clusters.title: Alternate task types in usability tests
clusters.rule: Alternate physically demanding tasks with stationary ones to avoid exerting older participants excessively.

clusters.title: Do not rely on accessibility widgets alone
clusters.rule: Do not rely on accessibility widgets alone; design products so screen-reader users can sequentially access content.

clusters.title: Disability and neurodiversity affect many
clusters.rule: Recognize 15–20% of the world's population lives with disability and 15–20% is neurodiverse; exclude them at risk.

findings.finding: 15-20% with disability; 15-20% neurodiverse

clusters.title: Accessibility is a mindset not checklist
clusters.rule: Treat accessibility and inclusivity as mindsets, not checklists or procedures; they are branches of usability.

clusters.title: Design visual treatments for all users
clusters.rule: Design visual treatments that help both sighted and vision-impaired users find, see, and understand information.

clusters.title: Screen readers experience linear interface
clusters.rule: Screen-reader users experience a linear interface; design products to make sense sequentially.

clusters.title: Design for neurodivergent executive function
clusters.rule: Design for simplicity, clarity, control, and support to help neurodivergent users manage executive-function challenges.

clusters.title: Check glassmorphic contrast carefully
clusters.rule: Check glassmorphic text contrast against multiple background colors; contrast may vary across complex areas.

clusters.title: Speak technical information clearly
clusters.rule: Speak technical information at half normal speed and offer options to repeat or receive via text.

clusters.title: End alt text with period for pause
clusters.rule: End alt text with a period to signal screen readers to pause, even for fragments.

clusters.title: Avoid jargon and abbreviations in alt text
clusters.rule: Avoid technical jargon and abbreviations in alt text unless users will certainly understand them.

clusters.title: Reanalyze alt text for each context
clusters.rule: Never reuse alt text for the same image across contexts; reanalyze the context each time.

clusters.title: Mention identity only if relevant
clusters.rule: Mention people's identity only if race, ethnicity, gender, religion, or culture is relevant to the image's purpose.

clusters.title: Edit page copy to avoid complex alt text
clusters.rule: For complex images, edit page copy to state the message as a list or table, avoiding lengthy alt text.

clusters.title: Prioritize captions and page copy
clusters.rule: Prioritize large-font captions and informative page copy over alt text for users with low vision.

clusters.title: Provide multiple recovery options
clusters.rule: Provide multiple recovery options for locked-out users that do not depend on the same device or method.

clusters.title: Build safety features from ground up
clusters.rule: Build safety features, blocking, and reporting mechanisms from the ground up, not as reactive afterthoughts.

clusters.title: Allow extra time for processing
clusters.rule: Allow extra time for users with language barriers or disabilities to process rapidly changing screens.

clusters.title: Never override platform shortcuts
clusters.rule: Never override platform-standard shortcuts like copy, paste, select-all, and print to prevent errors.

clusters.title: Anticipate diverse user capabilities and access patterns, bu
clusters.rule: Anticipate diverse user capabilities and access patterns, building resilience into design through flexible and tolerant interfaces.

clusters.title: Use aria-labelledby for primary tooltip labels and aria-desc
clusters.rule: Use aria-labelledby for primary tooltip labels and aria-describedby for supplementary tooltips.

clusters.title: Build with accessibility best practices so the app works for
clusters.rule: Build with accessibility best practices so the app works for all merchants and their customers.

clusters.title: Allow personalized controls for accessibility while keeping
clusters.rule: Allow personalized controls for accessibility while keeping main shared context identical across participants.

clusters.title: Center perspectives at intersections of multiple diversity a
clusters.rule: Center perspectives at intersections of multiple diversity axes when designing inclusive features.

clusters.title: Use semantically correct markup and appropriate ARIA roles s
clusters.rule: Use semantically correct markup and appropriate ARIA roles so assistive technologies identify components correctly.

clusters.title: Manage focus visually and follow z-pattern (left to right, t
clusters.rule: Manage focus visually and follow z-pattern (left to right, top to bottom) for keyboard users.

clusters.title: Use plain, concise, consistent language to support all reade
clusters.rule: Use plain, concise, consistent language to support all readers and those learning English.

clusters.title: Provide alt text for avatars displayed without an adjacent n
clusters.rule: Provide alt text for avatars displayed without an adjacent name.

clusters.title: Label controls by name, not solely by shape, color, size, lo
clusters.rule: Label controls by name, not solely by shape, color, size, location, or sound.

clusters.title: If audio plays for more than 3 seconds, provide pause, stop,
clusters.rule: If audio plays for more than 3 seconds, provide pause, stop, or independent volume control.

clusters.title: Colocate styles with components
clusters.rule: Keep component styling next to code, not in distant files, for developer clarity.

clusters.title: Study guidelines to understand component use
clusters.rule: Consult Human Interface Guidelines and design resources to know when and why to use each component.

clusters.title: Abstract input hardware through common API
clusters.rule: Write input code once via a common API so it works across different controllers and hardware without remapping.

clusters.title: Use optical margins for symbol alignment
clusters.rule: Apply optical margins in symbol templates to ensure proper alignment when symbols display in lists and tables.

clusters.title: Provide three weight-matched symbol scales
clusters.rule: Offer three matching weights in custom symbols to adjust appearance across different UI contexts and sizes.

clusters.title: Use system share sheet for collaboration
clusters.rule: Use the system share sheet to help users begin collaboration in a familiar, consistent way.

clusters.title: Apply symbol variants across hierarchies
clusters.rule: Use the symbolVariant modifier on view hierarchies to apply fill or outline variants across nested components.

clusters.title: Prioritize high-level APIs for pointer events
clusters.rule: Use high-level pointer APIs over low-level ones; they offer polished, consistent behavior.

clusters.title: Maintain icon identity over time
clusters.rule: Refine icon design deliberately and preserve lineage across versions rather than changing icons frequently.

clusters.title: Include three visual states for buttons
clusters.rule: Provide normal, pressed, and disabled states for all buttons and controls to prevent confusion.

clusters.title: Show disabled state to signal future availability
clusters.rule: Use disabled state instead of hiding controls so users understand location and when actions become available.

clusters.title: Teach design-to-code translation
clusters.rule: Provide code generation and design-to-code mapping to teach how design concepts translate to implementation.

clusters.title: Allow rich content in select buttons
clusters.rule: Use ::selectedcontent pseudo-element to display icons, images, or rich content in select buttons, not just text.

clusters.title: Customize selects with base appearance
clusters.rule: Apply appearance: base-select to customize select menus with CSS while preserving semantic HTML and accessibility.

clusters.title: Export icons at full canvas size
clusters.rule: Export icon layers at full canvas size to preserve geometry and relative positioning when importing into Icon Composer.

clusters.title: Use event-driven prototyping
clusters.rule: Use event-driven Script Graphs to prototype interactive logic without writing code.

clusters.title: Use variable overrides per instance
clusters.rule: Apply variable overrides per component instance to vary behavior while sharing the same script logic.

clusters.title: Prefer symbols in vertical bars
clusters.rule: Use symbol-only items in vertical bars to conserve space; provide icon and title so the system chooses representation.

clusters.title: Keep items on same axis with axisBehavior
clusters.rule: Use axisBehavior API to keep related items on the same axis; configure for symbol-text transitions or custom layouts.

clusters.title: Derive button shapes from device curvature
clusters.rule: Craft button shapes to harmonize with the device's curved display using hardware curvature, not simple pills.

clusters.title: Limit Liquid Glass to important elements
clusters.rule: Reserve Liquid Glass for the most important, interactive elements that users touch directly.

clusters.title: Use containerRelative glass corners
clusters.rule: Configure glass corners to automatically adapt to their container's corners with containerRelative settings.

clusters.title: Size glass elements for opacity and adaptation
clusters.rule: Larger glass sizes render more opaque; smaller sizes render clearer and adapt to light or dark mode automatically.

clusters.title: Remove custom backgrounds from sheets
clusters.rule: Remove custom backgrounds from sheets to let the new Liquid Glass material display properly.

clusters.title: Group glass elements with shared sampling
clusters.rule: Use glassEffectContainer to group multiple glass elements so they share a consistent sampling region.

clusters.title: Limit icon complexity to four groups
clusters.rule: Use four or fewer groups of up to four layers each per icon to maintain visual complexity within optimal bounds.

findings.finding: up to 4 groups per icon

clusters.title: Keep source icons flat and simple
clusters.rule: Keep source icon artwork flat, opaque, and simple; add dynamic effects like blur and shadow only in Icon Composer.

clusters.title: Add gesture targets for RealityKit
clusters.rule: Add both InputTargetComponent and CollisionComponent to gesture targets in RealityKit so interactions are recognized.

clusters.title: Replace text-icon pairs with symbol-badge
clusters.rule: Replace text plus icon pairs with symbol plus badge patterns to reduce vertical bar width and preserve space.

clusters.title: Use standard Watch widget layouts
clusters.rule: Use standard design layouts for Watch widgets to ensure visual consistency and smooth reading experience.

clusters.title: Use Automatic rendering mode for symbols
clusters.rule: Use Automatic rendering mode for symbols; it selects the mode that best highlights each symbol's characteristics.

clusters.title: Use Variable Color for states not depth
clusters.rule: Use Variable Color to represent sequential states or strength levels in symbols, not to create visual depth.

clusters.title: Show correct button glyph for controller
clusters.rule: Display the correct button glyph for the controller the player is holding, even after they remap buttons.

clusters.title: Preserve paths across symbol variants
clusters.rule: Maintain the number and order of paths across all design variants when supporting multicolor or hierarchical modes.

clusters.title: Convert live strokes to paths
clusters.rule: Convert live strokes to paths in symbol designs to enable colors and hierarchy groups to be applied later.

clusters.title: Use system-provided colors in multicolor symbols
clusters.rule: Use system-provided colors in multicolor symbols so they adapt to light mode, dark mode, contrast, and vibrancy.

clusters.title: Design AR buttons for one-handed use
clusters.rule: Design AR buttons for one-handed thumb use with high contrast and oversized icons at arm's length.

clusters.title: Limit small widgets to four items
clusters.rule: Limit small widgets to maximum four pieces of information to avoid overcrowding and preserve glanceability.

clusters.title: Use More button for secondary actions
clusters.rule: Use a More button with an ellipsis in a circular container for secondary actions in glanceable, non-scrolling views.

clusters.title: Use toolbar button API sparingly
clusters.rule: Use the toolbar button API sparingly, only in scrolling views for essential actions not primary to the view.

clusters.title: Collapse search with NSSearchToolbarItem
clusters.rule: Use NSSearchToolbarItem to collapse search into a button when window space is constrained.

clusters.title: Enable customization in iMessage apps
clusters.rule: Enable users to create and customize content within iMessage apps to increase engagement and feature discovery.

clusters.title: Use cards only for entry-level information
clusters.rule: Use cards only for entry-level information; avoid cards for dense, repetitive content—use tables or data lists.

clusters.title: Link selectable card titles
clusters.rule: Make card titles linked when cards are selectable or clickable to signal interaction to users.

clusters.title: Use one primary button per page
clusters.rule: Use primary buttons sparingly; never place more than one in a button group, rarely more than one per page.

clusters.title: Reserve button sizes for context
clusters.rule: Use medium button size for most interfaces; reserve small for compact spaces and large to emphasize sparingly.

clusters.title: Add leading visuals to buttons
clusters.rule: Add leading visuals like icons to buttons to provide context for button actions and improve comprehension.

clusters.title: Use danger buttons for destructive actions
clusters.rule: Use danger buttons for destructive actions that could harm or lose user data.

clusters.title: Use radio buttons for single selection
clusters.rule: Use radio buttons, not checkboxes, when only one option can be selected from a list.

clusters.title: Avoid dropdowns for two options
clusters.rule: Do not use a dropdown when there are only two options; use radio buttons instead.

clusters.title: Use widely recognized symbols
clusters.rule: Use widely recognized symbols and established visual metaphors to ensure universal icon understanding.

clusters.title: Design icons with straight-on perspective
clusters.rule: Use straight-on perspectives; avoid diagonal 3D shapes that confuse users at small icon sizes.

clusters.title: Size icons at 16px and 12px defaults
clusters.rule: Use 16×16px medium icons as default; reserve 12px icons for chevrons and dense compact elements.

clusters.title: Allow custom rendering in dropdowns
clusters.rule: Allow custom rendering of selected items and dropdown options to improve design flexibility.

clusters.title: Use shape to distinguish avatar types
clusters.rule: Use circles for individual people and squares for non-human entities like bots, teams, or organizations.

clusters.title: Scale avatars at standard increments
clusters.rule: Scale avatars at 16px base increments to 32px, then 8px increments to 64px maximum.

clusters.title: Display keyboard shortcuts as trailing visuals
clusters.rule: Display keyboard shortcuts as trailing visuals to help power users invoke frequent actions quickly.

clusters.title: Add borders between fluid buttons
clusters.rule: Add a 1px border between all fluid buttons using the button-separator token for distinction and accessibility.

findings.finding: 3:1 distinction between interactive elements

clusters.title: Auto-position tooltips by default
clusters.rule: Use auto-positioning for tooltips by default to detect browser edges and avoid cutoff.

clusters.title: Add trust badges near payments
clusters.rule: Add trust badges and security icons near payment buttons to reduce checkout anxiety and boost sales.

clusters.title: Use social proof badges
clusters.rule: Use social proof badges like bestseller status on products to increase purchase intent and trust.

findings.finding: sales increased X.X%

clusters.title: Write longer, benefit-focused labels
clusters.rule: Write longer button labels with clearer benefits instead of shorter, generic ones that lack specificity.

clusters.title: Prefix link labels with action verbs
clusters.rule: Prefix link labels with action verbs to encourage interaction; 'Play factory video' outperforms 'factory video'.

clusters.title: Replace scrollbars with thumbnails
clusters.rule: Replace scrollbars with clickable thumbnails for product image navigation to improve usability.

clusters.title: Make buttons visually prominent
clusters.rule: Replace text links with visually prominent buttons to increase clicks and user progression through flows.

clusters.title: Use high-contrast buttons for CTAs
clusters.rule: Use higher contrast buttons instead of low-contrast links for call-to-action elements to improve visibility.

clusters.title: Replace category links with tiles
clusters.rule: Replace category text links with tile images and increase font size to drive clicks and checkouts.

clusters.title: Make add-to-cart buttons large
clusters.rule: Make add-to-cart buttons larger, not smaller, to improve conversions and prominence.

findings.finding: Smaller add-to-cart button was rejected

clusters.title: Optimize button size for context
clusters.rule: Avoid making buttons so large they dominate the page; optimize button size for the specific context.

clusters.title: Use concrete, familiar button language
clusters.rule: Use concrete, familiar words over abstract verbs or emphatic adverbs in button labels.

clusters.title: Style month navigation buttons clearly
clusters.rule: Style month navigation buttons with defined borders to make them appear clearly clickable.

clusters.title: Increase date picker width
clusters.rule: Make date picker components wider to increase button size and padding for better interaction.

clusters.title: Widen product option buttons
clusters.rule: Make product option buttons wider and rectangular rather than small squares to improve usability.

clusters.title: Place option info inside buttons
clusters.rule: Place option labels and prices inside buttons rather than outside as subheadlines for clarity.

clusters.title: Apply light background to secondary buttons
clusters.rule: Give secondary buttons a light background fill instead of ghost-button styling for better visibility.

clusters.title: Use rounded corners on thumbnails
clusters.rule: Use rounded corners and light grey backgrounds on product thumbnails to improve visual appeal and density.

clusters.title: Test compound variation interactions
clusters.rule: Test compound variations that combine successful elements from multiple earlier variations to detect interactions.

clusters.title: Show online-now badges instead of response times
clusters.rule: Show online-now badges instead of average response times to improve trust and lead generation on marketplaces.

clusters.title: Suggest multiple affordances
clusters.rule: Design interfaces to suggest multiple affordances for common objects; avoid implying single purposes.

clusters.title: Use buttons to highlight important actions
clusters.rule: Use buttons to draw attention to important actions with a large, selectable surface area.

clusters.title: Set aria-expanded correctly on accordions
clusters.rule: Set aria-expanded true when an accordion panel is visible, false when hidden.

clusters.title: Include close button and escape key
clusters.rule: Include a visible close button in dialogs; allow Escape key to close for accessibility and user control.

clusters.title: Use details for single sections only
clusters.rule: Use details instead of tabs or accordions only when displaying a single section of content.

clusters.title: Use inset text sparingly
clusters.rule: Use inset text sparingly to differentiate blocks like quotes, examples, or additional information.

clusters.title: Use Warning text for critical information
clusters.rule: Do not use inset text for very important information; use Warning text component for legal or critical content.

clusters.title: Use Panel for interruption pages only
clusters.rule: Use Panel component only to highlight important content on confirmation or interruption pages, never elsewhere.

clusters.title: Do not make tags interactive
clusters.rule: Do not make tags interactive as users are unlikely to identify them as clickable elements.

clusters.title: Use lowercase i for optional info
clusters.rule: Use the lowercase i icon for optional, nice-to-know information that supplements understanding.

clusters.title: Recognize kebab and meatball icons
clusters.rule: Recognize kebab and meatball icons signal hidden options when used consistently across interfaces.

clusters.title: Prioritize native smartwatch apps
clusters.rule: Prioritize native smartwatch apps over third-party ones; 80% of smartwatch interactions occur in native apps.

findings.finding: 80% of interactions in native apps vs. third-party apps

clusters.title: Keep badge copy brief
clusters.rule: Keep badge copy brief—1–2 words for text, numbers for counts—to communicate meaning at a glance.

clusters.title: Limit badges per product
clusters.rule: Limit badges per product to retain their highlight function; overuse dilutes value and causes users to ignore.

clusters.title: Use design patterns for standardization
clusters.rule: Use design patterns to standardize, reuse solutions, create consistency, and reduce design and development time.

clusters.title: Document patterns with examples
clusters.rule: Document design patterns clearly with explanations, real-world examples, and guidance on variations.

clusters.title: Use accordions to organize content
clusters.rule: Use accordions to compress and organize content, especially helpful on mobile devices for space savings.

clusters.title: Use carousels to save space
clusters.rule: Use carousels to save screen space by fitting many items in a small area with manual or automatic rotation.

clusters.title: Reveal keyboard shortcuts gradually
clusters.rule: Reveal keyboard shortcuts and accelerators gradually as users become familiar with core interface functionality.

clusters.title: Test icons with users
clusters.rule: Test icons with users to verify both recognizability and correct interpretation of meaning.

clusters.title: Maintain design systems with dedicated teams
clusters.rule: Establish a dedicated team to maintain design systems continuously; without oversight, systems become outdated.

clusters.title: Avoid sliders for precise values
clusters.rule: Avoid sliders when users need to select a precise value; use them only for approximate ranges.

clusters.title: Place slider labels above or beside
clusters.rule: Place slider labels above or beside the control, never below, so they remain visible when the user's finger obscures.

clusters.title: Use icon-triggered search cautiously
clusters.rule: Use icon-triggered search cautiously; reduced prominence causes users to miss the feature entirely.

clusters.title: Provide detailed AI prototyping prompts
clusters.rule: Provide AI prototyping tools with detailed prompts describing layout, interactions, edge cases, and error states.

clusters.title: Keep simple interactions simple; make complex tasks possible
clusters.rule: Keep simple interactions simple; make complex tasks possible without adding unnecessary complexity.

clusters.title: Ensure every interface element contributes positively to the
clusters.rule: Ensure every interface element contributes positively to the larger system; eliminate isolated features.

clusters.title: Design with vectors and modular systems so designs adapt to
clusters.rule: Design with vectors and modular systems so designs adapt to any screen size or environment instead of breaking in wrong contexts.

clusters.title: Structure icons with distinct layers representing depth to e
clusters.rule: Structure icons with distinct layers representing depth to enable dynamic material effects like glass properties and lighting.

clusters.title: Use round shapes and avoid sharp edges to guide eye focus to
clusters.rule: Use round shapes and avoid sharp edges to guide eye focus to element centers and improve targeting accuracy.

clusters.title: Convert secondary text links to button styles for improved v
clusters.rule: Convert secondary text links to button styles for improved visibility and engagement.

clusters.title: Increase button padding and size to make primary actions mor
clusters.rule: Increase button padding and size to make primary actions more prominent and easier to interact with.

clusters.title: Remove borders from components to reduce visual clutter and
clusters.rule: Remove borders from components to reduce visual clutter and simplify the interface.

clusters.title: Apply high-contrast filled button style to primary search ac
clusters.rule: Apply high-contrast filled button style to primary search actions to boost completion rates significantly.

clusters.rule: Keep info-tip content inline or adjacent to the element it supports; avoid modals, overlays, or new pages that disconnect users from workflow.

clusters.title: Mark significant UI changes
clusters.rule: Mark significant UI changes with strong visual cues to overcome change blindness; subtle changes go unnoticed.

clusters.title: Stay neutral on feedback
clusters.rule: Stay neutral about outcomes; avoid encouraging language that teaches participants to perform for approval.

clusters.title: Design short feedback surveys
clusters.rule: Keep feedback surveys short, easy to complete, and enable users to provide detailed experience comments.

clusters.title: Use indicators for dynamic content
clusters.rule: Use indicators—visual cues like icons, color, or animation—to highlight dynamic content or UI elements that require attention.

clusters.title: Write concise transactional messages
clusters.rule: Write concise, easy-to-digest transactional messages; verbose content damages user trust in your brand.

clusters.title: Warn before presenting details
clusters.rule: Warn callers and give them time to prepare before presenting detailed information like phone numbers or emails.

clusters.title: Confirm caller selections
clusters.rule: Provide brief auditory confirmation when callers make a selection to show the system registered their choice.

clusters.title: Signal more content below
clusters.rule: Add scrolling cues at viewport edges to prevent illusion of completeness and signal more content below.

clusters.title: Handle asynchronous collaboration
clusters.rule: Design collaborative features to handle slow connections, real-time conflicts, and asynchronous editing with clear conflict resolution.

clusters.title: Signal changes with visual strength
clusters.rule: Signal changes far from the user's current focus with stronger visual cues than simple replacement.

clusters.title: Show immediate visual feedback
clusters.rule: Show immediate visual feedback for all actions; users assume unacknowledged clicks failed and try again.

clusters.title: Show progress on device tasks
clusters.rule: Display time remaining or completion percentage during long device tasks so users know progress and trust the device is working.

clusters.title: Repeat items for purchase commitment
clusters.rule: Repeat selected items in subsequent screens to establish continuity and reinforce commitment to the purchase.

clusters.title: Validate selection options
clusters.rule: Add validation copy for size or option selections to reduce returns and build purchase confidence.

clusters.title: Change button state after click
clusters.rule: Change button state to confirmation after user clicks, with link to next step to guide progression.

clusters.title: Organize action sequences into grouped tasks with a clear be
clusters.rule: Organize action sequences into grouped tasks with a clear beginning, middle, and end plus completion feedback.

clusters.title: Show affordance that content is slidable: use a focus style
clusters.rule: Show affordance that content is slidable: use a focus style and ensure the rightmost item is partially cut off.

clusters.title: Avoid forcing sound and video on launch; allow users to invo
clusters.rule: Avoid forcing sound and video on launch; allow users to invoke audio after content appears.

clusters.title: Show working prototypes or videos to stakeholders instead of
clusters.rule: Show working prototypes or videos to stakeholders instead of static mockups to communicate intent and spark conversations about constraints.

clusters.title: Show applied filter labels to reveal what conditions are bei
clusters.rule: Show applied filter labels to reveal what conditions are being filtered on.

clusters.title: Do not include critical information in tooltips; use always-
clusters.rule: Do not include critical information in tooltips; use always-visible helper text for essential task information.

clusters.title: Never place interactive elements inside tooltips; use toggle
clusters.rule: Never place interactive elements inside tooltips; use toggletips for buttons, links, or images instead.

clusters.title: Show tooltip only on hover or focus, hiding it when the user
clusters.rule: Show tooltip only on hover or focus, hiding it when the user moves away, for brief supplemental information.

clusters.title: Show 50% of the last option's height in menu overflow to sig
clusters.rule: Show 50% of the last option's height in menu overflow to signal more content; start scrolling at the sixth option.

findings.finding: Scroll starts at option 6

clusters.title: Avoid infinite scroll, autoplay, pull-to-refresh, streaks, d
clusters.rule: Avoid infinite scroll, autoplay, pull-to-refresh, streaks, daily rewards, and variable rewards that exploit compulsive behaviour.

clusters.title: Show stale data indicators when background synchronization i
clusters.rule: Show stale data indicators when background synchronization is in progress to maintain transparency.

clusters.title: Show online status badges or recent activity timestamps besi
clusters.rule: Show online status badges or recent activity timestamps beside listings to build trust.

findings.finding: +10.9% leads

clusters.title: Standardize typography across interfaces
clusters.rule: Use consistent sequences, terminology, colors, layout, fonts, and capitalization throughout interfaces.

clusters.title: Design clear type hierarchy
clusters.rule: Design type hierarchy and scale so merchants can easily find the information they need.

clusters.title: Use bold left-aligned type for clarity
clusters.rule: Use bolder, left-aligned typography in alerts and onboarding to strengthen clarity and readability.

clusters.title: Consolidate repeated typographic elements
clusters.rule: Standardize repeated elements (typography sizes, spacing, colors) into one style instead of maintaining multiple near-identical versions.

clusters.title: Maintain consistent header sizing and positioning
clusters.rule: Use tiered header sizes based on each tab's purpose while keeping titles consistently positioned across tabs.

clusters.title: Set optimal line length for readability
clusters.rule: Set line length to 14–16px text width via grid column sizing for optimal readability.

clusters.title: Use large titles for glanceability
clusters.rule: Use large titles in watchOS to improve glanceability and establish clearer hierarchy.

clusters.title: Enable rich typographic customization
clusters.rule: Use variable typefaces with continuous scaling for weight, width, and corner softness to enable rich customization without limiting to preset styles.

clusters.title: Enlarge important text for attention
clusters.rule: Use larger text in snippets to draw attention to important information; text is larger than system defaults.

clusters.title: Design widgets for glanceable legibility
clusters.rule: Design widgets for glanceable legibility from across the room when wall-mounted.

clusters.title: Remove unnecessary words from UI copy
clusters.rule: Remove unnecessary adverbs and adjectives from UI copy; they often function as fillers without adding clarity.

clusters.title: Remove unnecessary interjections from messages
clusters.rule: Remove interjections and pleasantries like "oops," "sorry," and "thank you" from error messages and alerts unless they add meaning.

clusters.title: Use exclamation points sparingly
clusters.rule: Use exclamation points sparingly, reserving them for genuinely celebratory or urgent moments to maintain impact.

clusters.title: Ensure parameter summaries remain readable
clusters.rule: Ensure parameter summaries remain readable as sentences regardless of which option is selected.

clusters.title: Use width styles for space constraints
clusters.rule: Use width styles—Condensed, Compressed, or Expanded—to accommodate space constraints and stylistic needs in UI design.

clusters.title: Match font properties to hierarchy intent
clusters.rule: Match font weight and width choices to typographic hierarchy intent: neutral styles for balance, extreme proportions for emphasis and attention.

clusters.title: Design symbols with multiple weights
clusters.rule: Design symbols with multiple weights to match text styling and adapt to features such as accessibility bold on iOS.

clusters.title: Scale symbols with text styles
clusters.rule: Use text styles like body or caption with symbols so both text and symbols scale with dynamic type.

clusters.title: Vertically center symbols with text
clusters.rule: Vertically center symbols with text cap height and weight-match them so they appear consistent despite scaling differences.

clusters.title: Compensate symbol weight when scaling
clusters.rule: Compensate symbol weight when scaling to maintain optical consistency; small scales appear lighter and large scales bolder without adjustment.

clusters.title: Format shortcut parameter summaries
clusters.rule: Keep shortcut parameter summaries short, verb-first, and exclude app name; show optional parameters under Show More.

clusters.title: Make all text dynamic
clusters.rule: Make all text dynamic if possible; text that can grow should grow with user's font size setting.

clusters.title: Scale glyphs with text
clusters.rule: Scale glyphs and icons alongside text to maintain visual balance as text size grows.

clusters.title: Align symbols to text baseline
clusters.rule: Design symbols to sit on the same baseline as adjacent text, with invisible margins that ensure proper alignment.

clusters.title: Limit text styles per screen
clusters.rule: Limit text styles to two or three per screen to create clear hierarchy while maintaining visual consistency.

clusters.title: Use optical sizes for fonts
clusters.rule: Use optical sizes for fonts: smaller text needs wider letter-spacing and sturdier thin strokes for legibility.

clusters.title: Apply consistent tracking with optical sizes
clusters.rule: Apply tracking (letter-spacing) consistently with optical size changes to prevent abrupt spacing shifts at size transitions.

clusters.title: Use tracking API for spacing
clusters.rule: Use the tracking API instead of kerning to tighten truncated strings and preserve ligatures for consistent word rhythm.

clusters.title: Match Dynamic Type to watch case size
clusters.rule: Use Dynamic Type default categories matching watch case size: Small for 38mm, Large for 40–42mm, XLarge for 44mm.

clusters.title: Use monochrome icons in toolbars
clusters.rule: Use monochrome icon rendering in toolbars to reduce visual noise and emphasize app content.

clusters.title: Never use asterisks with tiny text
clusters.rule: Never use asterisks with tiny text; it subconsciously triggers distrust by evoking decades of deceptive TV infomercial conditioning.

clusters.title: Provide icon and title for toolbar items
clusters.rule: Always provide both icon and title for toolbar items; let the system choose symbol-only or text+icon based on available space.

clusters.title: Modulate voice qualities by situation
clusters.rule: Modulate four core voice qualities—clarity, simplicity, friendliness, helpfulness—by turning each up or down based on the situation to adjust tone.

clusters.title: Design watchOS details for glance clarity
clusters.rule: Design watchOS detail views to be unmistakable at a glance so they require no title for clarity.

clusters.title: Keep shortcut titles concise
clusters.rule: Make shortcut titles concise and avoid truncation; never include app name since it is shown separately.

clusters.title: Increase Arabic font size with Latin
clusters.rule: Increase Arabic font size by 10% when paired with uppercase Latin to compensate for optical size difference.

findings.finding: 10% increase in Arabic font size compensates for optical volume difference with uppercase Latin

clusters.title: Increase spacing for Arabic diacritics
clusters.rule: Increase vertical spacing in UI when using vocalization marks and diacritics in Arabic to prevent text clipping.

clusters.title: Use Compressed width for single lines
clusters.rule: Use Compressed width style only for single lines or display headlines; avoid for extended reading passages.

clusters.title: Pair extreme proportions for display
clusters.rule: Pair extreme weight and width proportions for expressive display styles; center styles for neutral voice.

clusters.title: Use Condensed width for narrow columns
clusters.rule: Use Condensed width to fit more text per line in narrow columns without sacrificing readability.

clusters.title: Keep achievement titles under 30 characters
clusters.rule: Keep achievement titles and descriptions under 30 characters for reliable display across devices.

clusters.title: Keep leaderboard titles under 30 characters
clusters.rule: Keep leaderboard titles under 30 characters to prevent truncation across all devices and accessibility settings.

clusters.title: Make text wrap instead of truncate
clusters.rule: Make text wrap and avoid truncation as content size increases; use full display width available.

clusters.title: Apply weight compensation when scaling
clusters.rule: Apply weight compensation when scaling symbols to maintain consistent stroke thickness across small, medium, and large scales.

clusters.title: Never specify fixed frames for symbols
clusters.rule: Never specify fixed frames for symbols; instead use text styles and point sizes so symbols resize with Dynamic Type.

clusters.title: Specify symbols using typographic points
clusters.rule: Specify symbols using typographic points like text, not screen dimensions, to ensure proper rendering at all sizes.

clusters.title: Design symbol weights across full range
clusters.rule: Design symbol weights to maintain detail and visibility across the full weight range from ultra-light to black.

clusters.title: Avoid small text styles on Mac
clusters.rule: Avoid small text styles like caption and footnote on Mac; bump up text size to remain legible after 77% scaling.

clusters.title: Apply readability margins on large screens
clusters.rule: Apply readability margins on larger screens to restrict line length; allow text size to adjust based on Dynamic Type settings without compromising layout.

clusters.title: Increase letter spacing at smaller sizes
clusters.rule: Increase letter spacing as point size decreases to maintain comfortable reading experiences at smaller sizes.

clusters.title: Create typographic contrast for hierarchy
clusters.rule: Create typographic contrast through size, weight, or style to guide attention and establish hierarchy in layouts.

clusters.title: Use sentence case capitalization
clusters.rule: Use sentence case for capitalization; capitalize only the first letter and proper nouns.

clusters.title: Keep message line length under 66 characters
clusters.rule: Keep message line length under 66 characters per line in empty states.

clusters.title: Choose productive or expressive type set
clusters.rule: Use productive type set for product spaces to maintain focus; use expressive set for editorial content.

clusters.title: Balance font weight and size carefully
clusters.rule: Balance font weight and size carefully; larger lighter weight can rank higher than smaller bold weight.

clusters.title: Use semibold sparingly
clusters.rule: Use semibold sparingly; reserve it for section headers, not long-form text.

clusters.title: Keep body text color neutral
clusters.rule: Keep body text color neutral; use primary blue only for actions and links.

clusters.title: Use responsive text with relative values
clusters.rule: Use responsive text with relative values (rem) for font size across different browser defaults.

clusters.title: Use correct heading levels with size difference
clusters.rule: Use correct heading levels and establish 2-4 size difference between heading levels for clear hierarchy.

clusters.title: Use minimum 16px for long-form text
clusters.rule: Use minimum 16px font size for long-form text; avoid using 12px except for fine print.

clusters.title: Use heavy body text instead of heading text
clusters.rule: Apply body text in components with heavier font weight instead of heading text for greater contrast.

clusters.title: Align type to box edge padding
clusters.rule: Always align type to the edge of box padding, never place type on the padding itself.

clusters.title: Use rem units for typography
clusters.rule: Use rem units for typography to support accessible browser zoom experiences.

clusters.title: Avoid color as sole emphasis method
clusters.rule: Avoid using color as the primary method of emphasis in text hierarchy.

clusters.title: Left-align text with ragged edges
clusters.rule: Left-align text with ragged right edges rather than justifying, centering, or right-aligning.

clusters.title: Use rem design tokens for accessibility
clusters.rule: Use rem design tokens to respect browser default font size for low-vision accessibility.

clusters.title: Create scannable section headings
clusters.rule: Create scannable section headings in large or bold text for efficient navigation.

clusters.title: Left-align text with sentence case
clusters.rule: Use sentence-style capitalization for headings, titles, labels, and UI elements.

clusters.title: Use sentence case for all text
clusters.rule: Use sentence case for all text; avoid all caps because it is difficult to read.

clusters.title: Use color for typographic emphasis
clusters.rule: Use color on text to create emphasis or de-emphasis within visual hierarchy, not as sole indicator of importance.

clusters.title: Limit body text line length
clusters.rule: Limit line length to 60–80 characters per line for comfortable reading of body text.

findings.finding: 60–80 characters or 10–12 words per line

clusters.title: Wrap button labels instead of truncate
clusters.rule: Make button labels wrap to a second line rather than truncate when space is insufficient.

clusters.title: Left-align button labels
clusters.rule: Left-align button labels, never center-align them even if the button is wide.

clusters.title: Top-align wrapped checkbox labels
clusters.rule: Let wrapped checkbox label text sit beneath the control aligned at the top, never vertically center it.

clusters.title: Never hide critical information
clusters.rule: Never hide critical information in small text, low contrast, or unexpected locations; use consistent hierarchy and prominence.

clusters.title: Choose typeface carefully
clusters.rule: Choose typeface carefully; optimal font varies by reader, not a single best font for all.

findings.finding: 117 word-per-minute difference between worst and best typeface

clusters.title: Test individual typeface optimization
clusters.rule: Assume readers' preferred fonts will not be their best; test individual typeface optimization.

clusters.title: Choose serif fonts for reading speed
clusters.rule: Choose serif fonts for slightly faster online reading speed over sans-serif.

clusters.title: De-emphasize currency and decimals
clusters.rule: Use smaller font size for currency symbols and decimal amounts to de-emphasize cost.

clusters.title: Make prices more visible
clusters.rule: Make prices more visible through larger font size and higher contrast color.

clusters.title: Align time labels with descriptions
clusters.rule: Align time labels directly with their corresponding descriptions to reduce informational mismatch.

clusters.title: Enlarge prices and form fields
clusters.rule: Enlarge price display, form fields, and review counts to increase visibility and scannability.

clusters.title: Increase price visibility and emphasis
clusters.rule: Increase price visibility by enlarging the total price and removing decimal points to emphasize whole dollar amounts.

clusters.title: Display discounts prominently
clusters.rule: Display discount percentages in larger text with high color contrast to prominently highlight savings.

clusters.title: Improve font legibility overall
clusters.rule: Improve font legibility through larger sizes, heavier weights on subheadings, and updated typefaces.

clusters.title: Avoid orphaned words in headlines
clusters.rule: Avoid orphaned words created by line breaks in headlines, as they reduce readability and can confuse users.

clusters.title: Increase category link font size
clusters.rule: Increase font size of category navigation links to improve scannability and trigger more searches.

clusters.title: Increase line spacing at smaller sizes
clusters.rule: Increase line spacing as a percentage when using smaller font sizes.

clusters.title: Re-check line spacing on font changes
clusters.rule: Re-check line spacing when changing font or font size to maintain readability.

clusters.title: Start with 17px mobile body font
clusters.rule: Start with 17px mobile body font size and adjust based on content density and readability.

clusters.title: Size secondary text appropriately
clusters.rule: Make secondary text 2px smaller than default paragraph text.

clusters.title: Validate readability on actual devices
clusters.rule: View font-size designs on actual mobile devices to validate readability.

clusters.title: Use sentence case for headings without punctuation
clusters.rule: Use sentence case for headings and labels, but do not add punctuation.

clusters.title: Support text spacing overrides
clusters.rule: Ensure content adapts without loss when line height is set to 1.5×, paragraphs to 2×, letter spacing to 0.12×, and word spacing to 0.16× font size.

clusters.title: Do not interfere with user text spacing
clusters.rule: Do not interfere with user overrides of text spacing to improve readability.

clusters.title: Use h1 as main page heading
clusters.rule: Use the first h1 as the main page heading, not the site name.

clusters.title: Use descriptive headings and labels
clusters.rule: Use descriptive headings and labels to help users understand page content organization.

clusters.title: Single-word labels for navigation
clusters.rule: A single word or character label suffices if it provides a clear navigational cue.

clusters.title: Include handmade design elements
clusters.rule: Include variable line weights, incomplete paths, visible brushstrokes, hand-lettered type, misalignment, and organic shapes in handmade designs.

clusters.title: Limit designs to three type sizes
clusters.rule: Limit designs to three type sizes to establish strong hierarchy without overwhelming the user.

clusters.title: Increase leading and shorten line length
clusters.rule: Increase leading and shorten line lengths to make dense text blocks easier to read and avoid user overwhelm.

clusters.title: Structure text with headings
clusters.rule: Structure text with headings and subheadings; absent these, users revert to inefficient F-pattern scanning.

clusters.title: Make subheadings stand out and descriptive
clusters.rule: Make subheadings visually stand out and descriptive so users engage in efficient layer-cake scanning.

clusters.title: Avoid overly bright subheadings
clusters.rule: Avoid making subheadings so bright or large they resemble ads; users will ignore them.

clusters.title: Prioritize first line of content
clusters.rule: Prioritize the first line of content; it receives more gazes than subsequent lines.

clusters.title: Emphasize first words of each line
clusters.rule: Emphasize first few words on the left of each line; they receive more fixations than words to the right.

clusters.title: Use scannable structure with headings
clusters.rule: Use scannable structure with headings and subheadings to break up text blocks.

clusters.title: Left-align for predictable reading
clusters.rule: Left-align text instead of center-aligning to create predictable reading patterns and reduce cognitive load.

clusters.title: Write at lower reading level
clusters.rule: Write at a 6th–8th grade reading level for general audiences to maximize comprehension across all literacy levels.

findings.finding: Users read only 20–28% of page text; lower reading level helps process information faster with less effort

clusters.title: Distinguish product attributes from title
clusters.rule: Distinguish product attributes from title using spacing, line breaks, and distinct styling.

clusters.title: Pair bold headlines with clean body fonts
clusters.rule: Pair bold, chunky headlines with clean, neutral body fonts like Roboto or Inter to maintain readability.

clusters.title: Use clear noticeable headings
clusters.rule: Use clear noticeable headings to break content into scannable sections.

clusters.title: Use bulleted lists and bold text
clusters.rule: Use bulleted lists and bold text to focus the eye on the most important information.

clusters.title: Bold important words for scanning
clusters.rule: Bold, color, or link important words to trigger spotted-pattern scanning over inefficient F-pattern.

clusters.title: Use meaningful headings for scanning
clusters.rule: Use meaningful headings and subheadings; the layer-cake pattern with headings is far more effective than F-pattern scanning.

clusters.title: Chunk content with subheadings
clusters.rule: Chunk content with subheadings and call-out points even for motivated readers seeking deep comprehension.

clusters.title: Maintain consistent visual hierarchy
clusters.rule: Use consistent visual treatment (typeface, color, size, or weight) to signal hierarchy between body text and subheadings without making subheadings resemble promotions.

clusters.title: Signal hierarchy with visual styling
clusters.rule: Use visual styling like headers and bold text to signal importance and help users locate new content sections.

clusters.title: Use numerals instead of spelled-out words
clusters.rule: Use numerals instead of spelled-out words when displaying numbers in digital copy.

clusters.title: Place important words in first words
clusters.rule: Place the most important words in the first two words of links and headlines to support scanning.

clusters.title: Format articles for trust and quality
clusters.rule: Format articles clearly; format is the second-largest driver of news site trust, explaining 12% of UX quality.

findings.finding: Format improvements increase SUPR-Q by 12 percentage points per standardized unit

clusters.title: Keep carousel metadata concise
clusters.rule: Reduce carousel metadata to three lines maximum for clarity.

clusters.title: Test color vision deficiency accessibility
clusters.rule: Test interfaces in color vision deficiency modes to ensure red, green, and yellow hues are distinguishable without relying on color alone.

clusters.title: Convert existing assets to Display P3 carefully
clusters.rule: Use Convert to Profile rather than Assign to Profile when converting assets to Display P3 to preserve design intent.

clusters.title: Achieve 4.5:1 contrast for tint colors across modes
clusters.rule: Verify tint colors achieve 4.5:1 contrast ratio between light and dark modes using a color contrast calculator.

findings.finding: 4.5:1 contrast ratio minimum

clusters.title: Move brand color to content, not controls
clusters.rule: Keep UI controls unobtrusive by moving brand color into the content area when using Liquid Glass or similar materials.

clusters.title: Adapt Liquid Glass to content darkness
clusters.rule: Make Liquid Glass automatically shift from light to dark based on underlying content as the user scrolls.

clusters.title: Test lighting on multiple devices and modes
clusters.rule: Test color and lighting perception on monitor and headset separately; offer multiple lighting modes for viewer choice.

clusters.title: Use Palette mode with contrasting colors
clusters.rule: Use Palette rendering mode with two or more contrasting colors to give symbol elements prominence and allow environmental customization.

clusters.title: Provide high contrast in distant viewing
clusters.rule: Use vibrant backgrounds and check contrast beyond standard ratios when content will be viewed from a distance.

clusters.title: Update colors for high contrast accessibility
clusters.rule: Adjust color tint or provide alternate assets when Increase Contrast accessibility setting is enabled.

findings.finding: Color contrast ratio of 4.5-to-1 is minimum acceptable; 7.5-to-1 greatly improves legibility

clusters.title: Use white text over difficult glass colors
clusters.rule: Apply white text or symbols over glass material colors when color options reduce text visibility.

clusters.title: Round percentage thresholds to whole numbers
clusters.rule: Round percentage thresholds to whole numbers to avoid rounding errors in symbol appearance.

clusters.title: Use gradients to enhance readability over images
clusters.rule: Add gradient or blur behind text on images to improve readability without disrupting the design.

clusters.title: Use categorical palette colors in sequence
clusters.rule: Apply categorical palette colors strictly as described in order to maximize contrast between neighboring elements.

clusters.title: Avoid gradients in sequential data palettes
clusters.rule: Never use gradients in place of sequential palettes; use gradients only to highlight extremes in single-category visualizations.

clusters.title: Use desaturated or extreme brightness backgrounds
clusters.rule: Use desaturated, very bright, or very dark background colors in data visualizations to support readability.

clusters.title: Reuse color if elements differ visually
clusters.rule: Use the same color if chart elements are already distinguished by position or another visual variable.

clusters.title: Use shades of one hue to reduce clutter
clusters.rule: Use shades of a single hue instead of different hues to minimize visual clutter in visualizations.

clusters.title: Saturate important categories, desaturate others
clusters.rule: Use more saturated colors for important categories and desaturate less important ones to guide reader focus.

clusters.title: Design clear color keys for visualizations
clusters.rule: Create color keys to help readers quickly understand what colored elements in visualizations represent.

clusters.title: Use direct labels instead of color keys
clusters.rule: Use direct labels instead of color keys when possible to reduce cognitive load and improve clarity.

clusters.title: Build consistent data visualization palettes
clusters.rule: Create a fixed color palette for data visualizations to build brand trust and consistency across products.

clusters.title: Start with 3-10 brand colors for visualization palettes
clusters.rule: Begin with 3-10 colors from brand or website colors for a basic data visualization palette.

findings.finding: YouGov found they could complete 90% of simple charts with a limited palette

clusters.title: Few hues with multiple shades for recognition
clusters.rule: Use few hues with multiple shades to achieve brand recognition that designers recognize after first exposure.

clusters.title: Avoid culturally conflicted color meanings
clusters.rule: Avoid color meanings that conflict with topic intent; use mixed or desaturated colors when unsure of cultural associations.

clusters.title: Define primary colors to reduce designer decisions
clusters.rule: Define primary colors explicitly; most organizations complete 90% of simple charts with only a few core hues.

findings.finding: 90% of simple charts completed with limited palette

clusters.title: Organize palette for speed and consistency
clusters.rule: Organize color palette order and primary colors to reduce designer decisions and speed up chart creation.

clusters.title: Pair selection colors with visual cues
clusters.rule: Pair selected colors with a visual cue like checkmark, underline, or border to avoid relying on color alone.

clusters.title: Alternate layers between white and gray
clusters.rule: In light themes, alternate layers between White and Gray 10; in dark themes, step lighter with each layer.

clusters.title: Never darken components below background
clusters.rule: Do not apply components darker than the background unless using high-contrast mode.

clusters.title: Avoid midtones in light themes
clusters.rule: Avoid use of midtones in light themes to maintain clear layering and visual hierarchy.

clusters.title: Use Spectrum's defined palette exclusively
clusters.rule: Use Spectrum's defined color palette exclusively to ensure consistency; never create custom colors.

clusters.title: Avoid high-contrast adjacent colors
clusters.rule: Avoid placing colors with high hue contrast and near-equal saturation adjacent to prevent visual vibration and depth illusions.

clusters.title: Use lighter neutrals to highlight focus areas
clusters.rule: Use lighter neutral colors on surfaces to highlight primary focus areas and establish visual hierarchy.

clusters.title: Reduce eye strain in dark mode
clusters.rule: In dark mode, shift shared colors in saturation and brightness to reduce eye strain and accommodate visual accessibility.

clusters.title: Avoid overusing brand colors on large surfaces
clusters.rule: Avoid overusing brand colors on large surfaces to preserve hierarchy and aid navigation clarity.

clusters.title: Maintain icon contrast in interactive states
clusters.rule: Maintain icon contrast in interactive states; verify no readability loss when changing button colors.

clusters.title: Use distinct color for primary call-to-action
clusters.rule: Use a distinct, reserved color for primary call-to-action buttons rather than achromatic colors used elsewhere.

findings.finding: High-contrast black button was rejected; orange button retained

clusters.title: Use filled buttons with high contrast
clusters.rule: Use filled buttons with high contrast instead of ghost buttons with thin borders.

findings.finding: Ghost button variant rejected; scored -0.5 repeatability as evidence pattern is getting worse

clusters.title: Use high-contrast complementary colors for primary actions
clusters.rule: Use high-contrast complementary colors for primary action buttons to maximize visibility and click-through.

findings.finding: Reducing the color contrast of the search button was identified as a negative change that likely hurt overall test performance.

clusters.title: Show green status indicators for engagement
clusters.rule: Display online status or recent activity timestamps in green text beside listings to increase engagement and conversions.

clusters.title: Cross out higher prices to anchor perception
clusters.rule: Show historically higher prices crossed out next to current prices to anchor perception and increase conversions.

clusters.title: Balance contrast to avoid overwhelm or monotony
clusters.rule: Balance contrast carefully: too much overwhelms users, too little makes designs feel monotonous and hard to navigate.

clusters.title: De-emphasize threat-related content
clusters.rule: Use visual hierarchy to de-emphasize threat-related or emotionally negative content to reduce fixation by anxious users.

clusters.title: Keep color usage consistent with conventions
clusters.rule: Do not assign new meanings to colors; keep color usage consistent with existing platform conventions.

clusters.title: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA button contrast
