clusters.rule: Test filter interactions with real data and user clicks, not static mockups, to discover actual behavior.

clusters.title: Place validation error messages near the problematic field a
clusters.rule: Place validation error messages near the problematic field and pair with an icon indicator to signal which input needs correction.

clusters.title: Gather user feedback without bias or defensiveness
clusters.rule: Show prototypes to users and gather feedback without defending, arguing, or dismissing observations.

clusters.title: Present findings as stories, not just data
clusters.rule: Present research findings as stories about user experiences because stories engage memory more powerfully.

findings.finding: fMRI study showed personal narratives triggered widespread brain activity across listeners, including regions for social reasoning, emotional processing, and memory, versus only auditory or language regions for technical manual excerpts.

clusters.title: Build diverse teams for breakthrough ideas
clusters.rule: Build diverse teams with different skillsets and perspectives to generate breakthrough ideas faster.

clusters.title: Hold regular check-ins with stakeholders
clusters.rule: Hold regular check-ins with users and stakeholders to measure progress and uncover misalignment.

clusters.title: Show prototypes and implementations to stakeholders
clusters.rule: Show prototypes and implementations to stakeholders rather than explaining designs with static mockups.

clusters.title: Use group sequential analysis for safety
clusters.rule: Use group sequential analysis to stop experiments early when harmful effects appear.

clusters.title: Prioritize decisions on data, not opinion
clusters.rule: Listen to customer behavior data from experiments, not to the highest-paid person's opinion.

clusters.title: Design experiments with adequate statistical power
clusters.rule: Design experiments with adequate sample size and statistical power to detect meaningful effects reliably.

clusters.title: Use realistic mock data in prototypes
clusters.rule: Use realistic mock data in prototypes because users scrutinize unfamiliar data for inconsistencies.

clusters.title: Use eyetracking with sufficient sample size
clusters.rule: Use at least 39 eyetracking participants per task to generate reliable aggregate heatmap data.

findings.finding: 39 participants minimum

clusters.title: Translate UX findings to business outcomes
clusters.rule: Translate UX findings into business outcomes—revenue, conversion, risk, or cost—matching stakeholder priorities.

clusters.title: Use multiple independent reviewers for audits
clusters.rule: Run evaluations with three to five independent reviewers briefed separately to reduce missed issues.

clusters.title: Use AI for survey coding with verification
clusters.rule: Use AI to code open-ended survey comments; verify consistency with human coders.

findings.finding: ChatGPT-5.6 achieved near-perfect self-consistency and matched human interrater agreement (kappas .632–.704 in 2023)

clusters.title: AI moderators underperform on context and trust
clusters.rule: Use human moderators; AI scored worse on context-aware follow-up and trust-building than humans.

findings.finding: AI moderator talked more and faster; no difference in word count from participants in think-aloud tasks

clusters.title: Establish survey content validity with experts
clusters.rule: Establish content validity by consulting experts to confirm survey items represent relevant content.

clusters.title: Use SUS for usability perception measurement
clusters.rule: Use SUS on small sample sizes (two or more users) for reliable perceived usability data.

clusters.title: Use 30–50 cards in card-sorting studies
clusters.rule: Use 30–50 cards in card-sorting studies to prevent fatigue while encouraging thoughtful groupings.

clusters.title: Pilot test card-sorting before full study
clusters.rule: Run a pilot test before full card-sorting study to validate card count and label clarity.

clusters.title: Use session behavior tools to validate audit findings
clusters.rule: Use session behavior tools to validate audit findings at scale and measure user impact proportion.

clusters.title: Use post-test questionnaires for system usability
clusters.rule: Use post-test questionnaires like SUS to measure perceived usability of entire systems.

clusters.title: Use post-task scales to identify problem areas
clusters.rule: Use post-task scales to identify problematic parts of a design.

clusters.title: Define target behaviors with specificity
clusters.rule: Define target behaviors with specificity—include what users do, when, and what completion looks like.

clusters.title: Triangulate insights across methods and roles
clusters.rule: Triangulate insights across multiple research methods and roles to reveal how work moves across systems.

clusters.title: Define success hotspots and measure completion
clusters.rule: Define success hotspots on interfaces and code clicks within them to measure task completion.

clusters.title: Do not use employee usage as user research
clusters.rule: Do not substitute employee usage for user research; employees know too much to represent real users.

clusters.title: Interpret SUS scores using normalized database
clusters.rule: Interpret SUS scores by comparing them to percentile ranks from a normalized database of 10,000+ responses.

findings.finding: Average SUS score is 68th percentile; scores above 68 are above average, below 68 are below average.

clusters.title: Ask follow-up on difficult SEQ ratings
clusters.rule: When users rate a task below 5 on the SEQ, ask them to describe why they found it difficult.

clusters.title: Compare difficulty ratings across competing products
clusters.rule: Compare task difficulty ratings across competing products to isolate design friction from task complexity.

findings.finding: Users rate task difficulty 14% of the time inconsistently with actual task failure; differences average out across tasks.

clusters.title: Use numeric scales to measure abstract concepts
clusters.rule: Use linear numeric scales to measure abstract concepts like satisfaction, ease, and likelihood to recommend.

clusters.title: Use fixed subsets instead of forced ranking
clusters.rule: For long lists of 10+ items, use fixed-subset selection instead of forced ranking to reduce cognitive load.

clusters.title: Choose research method to match the question
clusters.rule: Choose research method to match the question, not the timeline or team familiarity.

clusters.title: Use 5-second tests to capture first impressions
clusters.rule: Conduct 5-second tests to capture users' initial visual impressions before they process details or read copy.

clusters.title: Avoid warning in 5-second tests
clusters.rule: Avoid warning participants in 5-second tests that designs will be shown briefly to capture authentic reactions.

clusters.title: Make design variations significantly different
clusters.rule: Make design variations in preference testing significantly different enough for nondesigners to detect immediately.

clusters.title: Counterbalance test variation order
clusters.rule: Counterbalance or randomize the order of design variations to prevent first-version bias in preference testing.

clusters.title: Present behavioral tasks before aesthetic questions
clusters.rule: Present behavioral tasks before aesthetic questions to avoid biasing task results with visual design.

clusters.title: Keep rating questionnaires short
clusters.rule: Keep numerical rating questionnaires short to reduce likelihood of random or unmotivated responses.

clusters.title: Use word-choice testing for brand perception
clusters.rule: Use closed word-choice testing to verify users perceive target brand attributes from design elements.

clusters.title: Use 50+ participants for quantitative tree testing
clusters.rule: Use 50+ participants per tree for quantitative tree testing to achieve narrow confidence intervals.

findings.finding: Sample size of 50+ per tree necessary for statistical significance in comparative studies.

clusters.title: Conduct pilot sessions before quantitative tree testing
clusters.rule: Conduct moderated pilot sessions before quantitative tree testing to verify task wording and catch nuances.

clusters.title: Use 11-point NPS scales consistently
clusters.rule: Use 11-point NPS scales consistently; switching to 10 or 5-point scales introduces scoring error.

findings.finding: Mean absolute difference of 4 percentage points between 11-point and 10-point scales; same for 5-point scales

clusters.title: Avoid 10-point NPS scales
clusters.rule: Avoid 10-point NPS scales; they reduce detractors by 8% without reducing promoters, inflating loyalty scores.

findings.finding: 8% reduction in detractors; 2.2% increase in promoters with 10-point scale

clusters.title: Budget for unmoderated consumer recruitment
clusters.rule: Budget $7–$10 per general consumer participant for unmoderated online panel recruitment.

findings.finding: $7–$10 general, $40–$100 specialized profiles; minimum project $1,500

clusters.title: Budget for moderated specialist recruitment
clusters.rule: Budget $100–$300 per qualified participant for external moderated recruitment, plus $12K–$15K for 20.

findings.finding: $100–$300 per qualified participant; $12K–$15K total for 20 moderated participants with qualifications

clusters.title: Budget more for international recruitment
clusters.rule: Budget $25 to $75 per participant for Western European and Asian recruitment, at least twice U.S. costs.

findings.finding: 2× U.S. costs; $25–$75 per participant in Western Europe and Asia

clusters.title: Use lower standard deviation for rating scales
clusters.rule: Use rating scale standard deviations of 20–28% of range instead of 50% for binary data.

findings.finding: Rating scales cut sample size 2–4× compared to binary metrics for same precision

clusters.title: Sample size for ±2-point margin on rating scales
clusters.rule: For ±2-point margin of error on 0–100 scale at 95% confidence, use n=603 instead of n=2,398.

findings.finding: Rating scales reduce sample size to 25% of binary metric requirement for ±2% margin of error

clusters.title: Estimate sample size with 20% standard deviation
clusters.rule: For multi-item questionnaires without historical data, use standard deviation of 20% of scale range.

clusters.title: Look at camera lens for perceived eye contact
clusters.rule: In remote sessions, look at the camera lens rather than the participant's video feed for perceived eye contact.

clusters.title: Encourage deeper conceptual thinking in card sorting
clusters.rule: Ask participants to subcategorize or combine cards when keyword matching occurs to encourage deeper thinking.

clusters.title: Allow iterative changes in card-sorting studies
clusters.rule: Allow participants to make iterative changes to groupings after initial sorting and ask about placement difficulty.

clusters.title: Recruit 15+ participants for qualitative card sorting
clusters.rule: Recruit at least 15 participants for qualitative card-sorting studies to understand reasoning.

findings.finding: minimum 15 participants for qualitative card sorts

clusters.title: Recruit 30–50 participants for quantitative card sorting
clusters.rule: Recruit 30–50 participants for quantitative card-sorting studies to ensure generalizable results.

findings.finding: 30–50 participants for quantitative card sorts to ensure generalizability

clusters.title: Ask follow-up questions after card sorting
clusters.rule: Ask follow-up questions after card sorting to understand rationale and label clarity issues.

clusters.title: Run moderated sessions with quantitative card sorting
clusters.rule: Run moderated card-sorting sessions alongside quantitative studies to understand reasoning.

clusters.title: Behavioral economics drives business performance
clusters.rule: Companies applying behavioral economics effectively can outperform peers by 85% in sales growth.

findings.finding: 85% sales growth improvement, 25% gross margin improvement

clusters.title: Observe expert users in actual environment
clusters.rule: Observe expert users working in their actual environment, not in labs, to discover contextual factors.

clusters.title: Use scenario interviews with domain experts
clusters.rule: Use scenario-based interviews and discussion with domain experts to assess reasoning, not just accuracy.

clusters.title: Evaluate against external standards for objectivity
clusters.rule: Evaluate against external standards to remove internal bias; familiarity blinds teams to friction.

clusters.title: Use research-backed audit standards
clusters.rule: Use research-backed audit standards so findings map to documented failure patterns.

clusters.title: Avoid keyword targeting on landing pages
clusters.rule: Keyword and operating-system targeting on landing pages does not reliably increase conversions.

clusters.title: Avoid relying on NPS as a one-size-fits-all metric; use it p
clusters.rule: Avoid relying on NPS as a one-size-fits-all metric; use it purposefully rather than as a blanket measurement.

clusters.title: Build design skills through repeated exposure to use cases s
clusters.rule: Build design skills through repeated exposure to use cases so you can recognize patterns and anticipate design problems.

clusters.title: Create a single source of truth for approved design delivera
clusters.rule: Create a single source of truth for approved design deliverables accessible to the entire team.

clusters.title: When testing prototypes with users, ask three questions: whe
clusters.rule: When testing prototypes with users, ask three questions: whether they understand how to perform the key interaction, whether it feels easy, and how they would improve it.

clusters.title: Test design changes with real users in qualitative studies b
clusters.rule: Test design changes with real users in qualitative studies before concluding why quantitative experiments failed, not after launching.

clusters.title: Seek real-world data and diverse user feedback rather than p
clusters.rule: Seek real-world data and diverse user feedback rather than projecting your own preferences onto product design decisions.

clusters.title: Recruit user research participants who represent the full ra
clusters.rule: Recruit user research participants who represent the full range of people using your service.

clusters.title: Document and share research findings with team members, mana
clusters.rule: Document and share research findings with team members, managers, and the public when appropriate.

clusters.title: Use attitudinal testing methods to evaluate brand alignment
clusters.rule: Use attitudinal testing methods to evaluate brand alignment and first impressions of visual design choices.

clusters.title: Use tree testing to validate an existing or proposed navigat
clusters.rule: Use tree testing to validate an existing or proposed navigation structure by testing content findability.

clusters.title: Match platform icon conventions
clusters.rule: Use icons that match platform-specific conventions while maintaining brand consistency across iOS, Android, and Web.

clusters.title: Full-width buttons on mobile
clusters.rule: Make buttons stretch full width on mobile to enable easier one-handed pressing and target accuracy.

clusters.title: Control slider label placement
clusters.rule: Place slider labels above or beside controls, not below, so users see them while dragging on touch.

clusters.title: Avoid stacked bottom sheets
clusters.rule: Do not stack multiple bottom sheets; overlapping sheets confuse users about interaction and dismissal patterns.

clusters.title: Optimize mobile checkout flow
clusters.rule: Surface cost, delivery, returns, and stock information early in mobile checkout to prevent late surprises and abandonment.

clusters.title: Benchmark mobile competitiveness
clusters.rule: Benchmark mobile checkout against industry median and top quartile to calibrate competitive performance.

clusters.title: Preserve user progress states
clusters.rule: Preserve filter states and cart contents when users navigate between mobile pages to prevent context loss.

clusters.title: Avoid disruptive inline ads
clusters.rule: Avoid inline ads within scrollable mobile content; they occupy too much screen and interrupt reading flow.

clusters.title: Group content to avoid scrolling
clusters.rule: Group mobile page content into collapsed sections to prevent endless scrolling and allow filter refinement.

clusters.title: Load products strategically
clusters.rule: Load 15 to 30 products before showing Load More; avoid lazy-loading all products at once on mobile.

clusters.title: Design for QR code context
clusters.rule: Link QR codes to mobile-friendly pages, not generic homepages; assume users scan and visit on mobile.

clusters.title: Crisis comms mobile-first format
clusters.rule: Write crisis communications in mobile-first format with short sentences and bulleted lists for quick scanning.

clusters.title: Disable motion-triggered functions
clusters.rule: Allow users to disable motion-triggered functions to prevent accidental activation on mobile devices.

clusters.title: Offer user profiles for shared devices
clusters.rule: Provide user profiles on shared devices to separate viewing histories and personalized recommendations.

clusters.title: Consistent platform accelerators
clusters.rule: Maintain accelerator consistency across web, mobile, and desktop so common shortcuts work identically everywhere.

clusters.title: Dedicated mobile UX audit attention
clusters.rule: Give mobile UX dedicated audit attention; mobile dominates retail visits but receives late, shallow testing.

findings.finding: Mobile generates ~75% of retail store visits

clusters.title: iMessage app personalization
clusters.rule: Design iMessage apps to be playful and personal, allowing users to express themselves uniquely and colorfully.

clusters.title: iMessage financial transactions
clusters.rule: Enable core financial transactions in iMessage without leaving conversation using Apple Pay for seamless commerce.

clusters.title: iMessage collaborative engagement
clusters.rule: Design collaborative iMessage apps to require and enable participation from both parties to create engagement.

clusters.title: Watch widget file optimization
clusters.rule: Scale PDF graphics automatically across watch sizes using 2x scale factor and Automatic property to reduce effort.

findings.finding: Scales down 9% for 38mm, up 10% for 44mm with one source file.

clusters.title: Remove Live Activities from lock screen after a short durati
clusters.rule: Remove Live Activities from lock screen after a short duration when they end to avoid manual dismissal.

clusters.title: Provide a floating reference point on mobile so users see co
clusters.rule: Provide a floating reference point on mobile so users see comparable plan information without scrolling up and down.

clusters.title: Create signature, recognizable product feel
clusters.rule: Focus design energy on signature experiences that connect products and give them a distinctively recognizable feel.

clusters.title: Avoid blending issues in layered designs
clusters.rule: Avoid large semitransparent regions in app icon layers to prevent unintended blending with shadows.

clusters.title: Use frontal perspectives and avoid 3D
clusters.rule: Use frontal, flat perspectives and avoid realistic 3D objects in icon designs as they compete with material glass effects.

clusters.title: Differentiate with unique, eye-catching artwork
clusters.rule: Display unique, eye-catching artwork to improve player or content differentiation.

clusters.title: Use real-world metaphors for adoption
clusters.rule: Use real-world object metaphors and skeuomorphic designs to ease adoption and user readiness.

clusters.title: Balance attribute salience across options
clusters.rule: Minimize salience of negative attributes on superior options; ensure positive attributes are equally prominent across all choices.

clusters.title: Match button appearance to function
clusters.rule: Ensure button appearance and role match its actual function.

clusters.title: Balance neobrutalism with usability
clusters.rule: Carefully balance neobrutalism's distinctive look with usability to avoid overwhelming or confusing interfaces.

clusters.title: Avoid ad-like design patterns
clusters.rule: Avoid design elements that resemble ads; users ignore content that signals advertising.

clusters.title: Design for all three pillars of delight
clusters.rule: Design for visceral, behavioral, and reflective pillars of delight, not just one or two, for lasting emotional connection.

clusters.title: Include natural visual elements
clusters.rule: Include natural visual elements like mountains, trees, or water; they spark more positive affect than urban imagery.

findings.finding: positive response to natural elements vs. urban landscapes

clusters.title: Credit human artists for trust
clusters.rule: Credit the human artist by name in all promotions of handmade designs; authorship is a trust signal distinguishing human work from AI.

clusters.title: Align visual design with product delivery
clusters.rule: Don't use warmth and handmade aesthetics to conceal product shortcomings; misaligned visual messaging undermines trust when product cannot deliver.

clusters.title: Make destructive actions recoverable
clusters.rule: Make destructive actions error-tolerant for users with limited motor control.

clusters.title: Use error pages for blocking errors
clusters.rule: Use error pages for primary errors that block task completion and prevent the expected page from loading.

clusters.title: Use error banners for secondary errors
clusters.rule: Display error banners for secondary errors that block current tasks but allow the expected page to load.

clusters.title: Show all errors at once
clusters.rule: Show all detected errors to users, not just the first one, to prevent repeated form resubmissions.

clusters.title: Confirm before destructive actions
clusters.rule: Check user input for errors and let users correct them before submission on important transactions.

clusters.title: Preserve form data on validation errors
clusters.rule: Never clear form fields when showing error messages; keep both passing and failing answers.

clusters.title: Announce errors to screen readers
clusters.rule: Move keyboard focus to the error summary when the page loads so screen readers announce it immediately.

clusters.title: Use specific file upload messages
clusters.rule: Use specific error messages for each file upload error condition.

clusters.title: Protect login credential security
clusters.rule: Never reveal whether username or password was wrong in login errors.

clusters.title: Use plain language on 404 pages
clusters.rule: Use straightforward plain language on 404 pages; include heading, explanation, fixes, actions, and support channels.

clusters.title: Minimize initial load time
clusters.rule: Load only minimum assets to reach first interactive screen; load remaining content asynchronously.

clusters.title: Hide background data loading
clusters.rule: Load additional data behind the scenes after installation without showing it to users.

clusters.title: Use spinners when structure unknown
clusters.rule: Use spinners instead of skeletons when content structure cannot be predicted.

clusters.title: Reduce structure uncertainty
clusters.rule: Show expected content structure in skeleton form to reduce anxiety about what is loading.

clusters.title: Exclude certain UI patterns from skeletons
clusters.rule: Never apply skeleton states to toasts, menus, dropdowns, modals, or loader components.

clusters.title: Match indicator scope to processing scope
clusters.rule: Use full-screen indicators for application-wide processing; use inline indicators for single-component processing.

clusters.title: Use progress bars instead of spinners
clusters.rule: Show progress bars to communicate what is happening and how long it will take.

clusters.title: Distinguish spinners from progress indicators
clusters.rule: Use progress indicators for processes exceeding a few seconds instead of indefinite looped spinners.

clusters.title: Provide accessibility feedback during loading
clusters.rule: Notify screen readers when application is loading, busy, stuck, or fails.

clusters.title: Show visible feedback quickly
clusters.rule: Display loading feedback within 50 milliseconds to prevent users interpreting the interface as broken.

findings.finding: 90% of users expect feedback within 50 milliseconds

clusters.title: Style skeletons for accessibility
clusters.rule: Use distinguishable colors and clear but undistracted animations in skeleton screens.

clusters.title: Provide cancellation for long processes
clusters.rule: Allow users to cancel long processes; do not hijack system control during waits over 10 seconds.

clusters.title: Triple wait tolerance with feedback
clusters.rule: Progress indicators increase wait tolerance threefold; users wait 3× longer with feedback.

findings.finding: Users willing to wait 3× longer with animated progress bar vs. no indicator

clusters.title: Show progress bars to make wait times tolerable, regardless
clusters.rule: Show progress bars to make wait times tolerable, regardless of their measured accuracy.

clusters.title: Use standard search iconography
clusters.rule: Use magnifying glass icon universally to signify search fields and maintain consistent user expectations.

clusters.title: Avoid search for small or simple data
clusters.rule: Do not implement search when dataset is small or information is easily found in a single view.

clusters.title: Support Enter to submit, Escape to clear
clusters.rule: Enable Enter key to submit search and Escape key to clear the field for efficient keyboard interaction.

clusters.title: Design no-results states clearly
clusters.rule: Display no-results view with search icon, title, subtitle, and echoed search text to help users catch typos and understand intent.

clusters.title: Guide search with example inputs
clusters.rule: Show example search inputs (ingredients, places, friends) on empty states to overcome blank-page paralysis and improve discoverability.

clusters.title: Avoid sequential field prompts on browse pages
clusters.rule: Do not auto-prompt for multiple sequential search fields on listing pages where users browse results passively.

clusters.title: Load 25–75 results without infinite scroll
clusters.rule: Load 25 to 75 results by default; never use infinite scrolling for search result pages.

clusters.title: Show popular results on zero matches
clusters.rule: Display popular or related products on empty search results rather than blank pages to improve conversion and guidance.

clusters.title: Implement type-ahead in large listboxes
clusters.rule: Enable type-ahead search in listboxes with more than seven options to reduce interaction steps and cognitive load.

clusters.title: Design AI tools for multiple constraints
clusters.rule: Use AI tools to handle multiple simultaneous constraints better than traditional keyword search for complex queries.

clusters.title: Recognize answers on results pages
clusters.rule: Recognize when users find complete answers on results pages without clicking through; satisfy intent at search results.

clusters.title: Combine search with navigation options
clusters.rule: Provide both search and navigation paths; search alone forces high cognitive effort in query construction.

clusters.title: Align suggestions to intent, not trends
clusters.rule: Align suggestions to user search intent, not exploration; avoid unrelated or trending items as autocomplete.

clusters.title: Placeholder text behavior in search fields
clusters.rule: Show placeholder text on focus; remove it only when user types to maintain visual clarity without hiding search intent.

clusters.title: Design for non-sequential scanning
clusters.rule: Design for variable attention distribution and non-sequential scanning; modern results require skimmable layouts and visual hierarchy.

clusters.title: Include alternatives alongside branded terms
clusters.rule: When using branded terminology, include plain language alternatives for SEO and user education in the same content.

clusters.title: Trust in ranking drives single-result selection
clusters.rule: Recognize that one in five searches end with a single-result selection; trust in ranking and top placement drives this behavior.

findings.finding: 20% of queries involve fixation on only one SERP element; statistically significant increase from 17% in 2006 (p < 0.001)

clusters.title: Use images as quick relevance signposts
clusters.rule: Include visual elements in search results to act as quick signposts that verify result relevance and guide scanning.

findings.finding: Users immediately corrected off-topic searches (e.g., snake photos for 'copperhead' instead of Civil War faction) when visual signposts clarified intent.

clusters.title: Mirror query expansion in featured snippets
clusters.rule: Design featured snippets to mimic natural language query expansion; show related questions without requiring reformulation.

findings.finding: Users clicked related questions in 'People Also Ask' because interaction cost was low (no page load) and benefit was high (answers already visible).

clusters.title: Redirect tasks via related-question accordions
clusters.rule: Use People Also Ask accordions to redirect user tasks; ensure loaded questions relate semantically to the clicked question.

findings.finding: One user searching for Botox cost saw 'Is Botox safe?' question, which changed her entire task goal to 'noninvasive approaches' after reading safety concerns.

clusters.title: Maintain consistent SERP layout across queries
clusters.rule: Use consistent layouts across different queries so users do not reassess page structure and can scan faster.

clusters.title: Place critical info below fold for research
clusters.rule: For research tasks, position critical information below the fold; research users explore deeply unlike fact-finders who click top results.

findings.finding: 20% of research-task selections below fold vs. 5% for fact-finding tasks

clusters.title: Teach advanced search operators via embedded boxes
clusters.rule: Embed site-specific search boxes in top results; display query syntax to teach advanced search operators for power users.

clusters.title: Minimize SERP decision time
clusters.rule: Limit decision time on results pages; users spend 5.7 seconds on average before selecting the first result.

findings.finding: Average 5.7 seconds (95% CI: 4.9–6.5) before first selection

clusters.title: Highlight search keywords in results to guide user attention
clusters.rule: Highlight search keywords in results to guide user attention and improve task completion.

findings.finding: 738,295 visitors tested, 80% statistical power at 1% MDE

clusters.title: Persist search queries in the input field to allow users to
clusters.rule: Persist search queries in the input field to allow users to easily refine and adjust searches without retyping.

clusters.title: Use icon-triggered or collapsed search cautiously; reduced p
clusters.rule: Use icon-triggered or collapsed search cautiously; reduced prominence may cause users to miss the search feature entirely.

clusters.title: Set row height to 40px default
clusters.rule: Use medium 40px row height as default; adjust for density or readability needs.

clusters.title: Enable row hover state for scanning
clusters.rule: Always enable row hover state to help users visually scan columns.

clusters.title: Concise column titles with tooltips
clusters.rule: Keep column titles to one or two words; wrap to two lines then truncate, showing full text in tooltip.

clusters.title: Match toolbar to table row height
clusters.rule: Match toolbar height to data table row height for visual alignment and consistency.

clusters.title: Use skeleton states for table loading
clusters.rule: Use skeleton states instead of spinners for tables with expected load time.

clusters.title: Persist overflow menu icons by default
clusters.rule: Persist overflow menu icons by default; only hide on hover if visual clutter is a priority.

clusters.title: Disable actions when batch mode active
clusters.rule: Disable single action icons and overflow menus when batch mode is active.

clusters.title: Use comparison tables for feature clarity
clusters.rule: Use comparison tables with checkmarks to make feature differences between plans clearer.

clusters.title: Add family product comparison tables
clusters.rule: Add product comparison tables mid-page showing related or family products with clickable thumbnails.

clusters.title: Progressive load for category products
clusters.rule: Show 10 to 30 products initially, lazy-load 10 to 30 more, then show Load More button at 50 to 100 products.

clusters.title: Use Load More over pagination
clusters.rule: Use Load More buttons instead of pagination or infinite scroll; users browse and read more products closely.

clusters.title: Show more results for better performance
clusters.rule: Showing more results on product pages generally performs better than showing fewer, all else equal.

clusters.title: Recency bias in sequence design
clusters.rule: Users recall final 2–3 items in a sequence with double the accuracy of middle items; design accordingly.

findings.finding: Probability of recall for first and last items can be up to 2x that of middle items

clusters.title: Use HTML table elements over ARIA
clusters.rule: Use HTML table elements instead of WAI-ARIA table role; test thoroughly with assistive technology if using ARIA.

clusters.title: Replace tables with grids for interactivity
clusters.rule: Replace tables with grids if they contain many interactive widgets to reduce the page tab sequence length.

clusters.title: Right-align numbers for comparison
clusters.rule: Right-align numbers in table cells to make comparison easier.

clusters.title: Consider alternatives to complex tables
clusters.rule: Consider alternatives to tables (summaries, lists, expanders, tabs) for complex data to reduce cognitive overload.

clusters.title: Do not use tables for page layout
clusters.rule: Avoid using tables to lay out page content; use a grid system instead.

clusters.title: Order columns by user importance
clusters.rule: Order table columns by user importance and group related columns adjacent to minimize eye movement.

clusters.title: Clarify cell-to-record association
clusters.rule: Ensure users always know what data cell belongs to which record in large tables.

clusters.title: Highlight key differences in comparison
clusters.rule: Use comparison tables or move differentiating features to the top when options differ on only a few attributes.

clusters.title: Append units to numerical values
clusters.rule: Always append units of measure to numerical values to prevent user confusion with metric versus imperial measurements.

clusters.title: Mobile-friendly table presentation
clusters.rule: Use collapsible sections or truncation on mobile instead of dense compression to avoid excessive scrolling.

clusters.title: Limit comparison products to five
clusters.rule: Limit compare tools to show no more than 5 products side by side; do not require more alternatives than working memory handles.

clusters.title: Show positive and negative attributes
clusters.rule: Show both positive and negative attributes for each alternative so users can determine whether benefits outweigh drawbacks.

clusters.title: Fix column headers for scanning
clusters.rule: Use fixed column headers so users never lose column identity while scanning comparison tables downward.

clusters.title: Allow hiding irrelevant products
clusters.rule: Let users hide irrelevant products in multi-column tables to preserve the lawn-mower scanning pattern.

clusters.title: Group yes/no rows for pattern flow
clusters.rule: Group Yes/No and checkmark rows together to avoid disrupting the lawn-mower pattern.

clusters.title: Move empty rows to table end
clusters.rule: Move empty or placeholder rows to the end of the table, never in the middle of active scanning content.

clusters.title: Measure spec sheet UX performance
clusters.rule: Measure and track spec sheet UX performance; 64% of ecommerce sites have poor or mediocre spec sheet design.

findings.finding: 64% of ecommerce sites' spec sheet UX performance is poor or mediocre

clusters.title: Apply inset style for readability
clusters.rule: Apply inset style to table views for improved readability: add horizontal and vertical padding around selections.

clusters.title: Set toolbar minimum width threshold
clusters.rule: Set minimum width threshold for displaying all toolbar controls in data grid.

clusters.title: Use table captions like headings to help users find, navigat
clusters.rule: Use table captions like headings to help users find, navigate, and understand tables.

clusters.title: Normalize interaction patterns
clusters.rule: Normalize all input methods—keyboard, mouse, callback events—into a single simple interface.

clusters.title: Three-phase interaction feedback
clusters.rule: Design feedback for before, during, and after interaction phases to guide user understanding.

clusters.title: Realistic content in prototypes
clusters.rule: Populate prototypes with edge cases: empty states, long text, unbounded lists, and variable content.

clusters.title: Preserve features across device poses
clusters.rule: Preserve all controls and functionality across every device pose; do not tie features to specific folds.

clusters.title: Interactive glass effects
clusters.rule: Set isInteractive to true on glass effects for views needing button-like scaling and bouncing.

clusters.title: Hide content surprises
clusters.rule: Show hover effects only from visible elements; hidden content revealed accidentally surprises users.

clusters.title: Auto-detect game controller input
clusters.rule: Auto-detect connected game controllers and switch input handling; do not require manual settings.

clusters.title: Smart Stack widget priority
clusters.rule: Prioritize Smart Stack widgets by time, location, headphones, sleep, or activity detection.

clusters.title: Show presence in shared content
clusters.rule: Display participant initials or names when others interact with shared content to reinforce presence.

clusters.title: Equal shared playback control
clusters.rule: Use shared playback controls without restrictions; everyone should feel able to control equally.

clusters.title: Filled symbols and accent for selection
clusters.rule: Use filled symbols in swipe actions and tabs to show selection with accent color emphasis.

clusters.title: Checkmarks for selected items
clusters.rule: Use checkmarks in menus to show the currently selected item in selection-based interactions.

clusters.title: Instant button state animation
clusters.rule: Animate button state changes instantly or very quickly to feel responsive; avoid slow fades.

clusters.title: Fluid drag cancellation
clusters.rule: Allow users to drag a finger outside a button to cancel activation before release.

clusters.title: Enlarge small control hit areas
clusters.rule: Make the hit area of small controls larger than their visual size to aid interaction.

clusters.title: Magnetic axis-constrained movement
clusters.rule: Constrain pointer movement along axes to guide users toward target rows or columns.

clusters.title: Pointer region padding and snapping
clusters.rule: Extend pointer region padding beyond control bounds so pointer snaps to targets early.

clusters.title: Seamless pointer region transitions
clusters.rule: Coordinate pointer region transitions across adjacent controls with contiguous regions and no gaps.

clusters.title: Direct actions in empty states
clusters.rule: Provide direct links or buttons in empty states to start key tasks that populate content.

clusters.title: Layered hover and pressed states
clusters.rule: Layer hovered and pressed states onto current state while keeping selected items recognizable.

clusters.title: Indeterminate checkbox state
clusters.rule: Use indeterminate state when a checkbox contains a sublist with some items selected.

clusters.title: Hide secondary buttons on hover
clusters.rule: Hide secondary buttons on hover rather than displaying them always to reduce visual clutter.

clusters.title: High contrast for selection
clusters.rule: Use higher visual contrast between selected and unselected product options.

clusters.title: Preserve predictability across session
clusters.rule: Only apply property changes when users restart the app; never change UI mid-session.

clusters.title: Trigger popups with focus and keys
clusters.rule: Hide popups by default; display them only when triggered by focus, arrow key, or button.

clusters.title: Focus destructive dialogs safely
clusters.rule: For dialogs with destructive final steps, set initial focus to the safest action.

clusters.title: Distinguish focused from selected
clusters.rule: Visually distinguish between focused and selected items in trees.

clusters.title: High contrast primary buttons
clusters.rule: Use high contrast between enabled buttons and the rest of design to catch attention.

clusters.title: Delay hover state to prevent accidents
clusters.rule: Add 150–200ms delay to hover state to prevent accidental color changes from mouse movement.

clusters.title: Desaturate disabled button appearance
clusters.rule: Display disabled buttons with reduced contrast and desaturated colors to signal they are not clickable.

clusters.title: Fast pressed state feedback
clusters.rule: Show pressed state feedback within 100–150ms so users perceive the action as instantaneous.

findings.finding: 100–150ms feedback prevents users from pressing buttons multiple times

clusters.title: Announce disabled state to screen readers
clusters.rule: Add ARIA-disabled attribute to disabled buttons so screen readers announce their inactive state.

clusters.title: Warning buttons for destructive actions
clusters.rule: Use warning buttons only for destructive actions that cannot be undone.

clusters.title: Tag labels use adjectives
clusters.rule: Use adjectives rather than verbs for tag labels to avoid users thinking they are clickable.

clusters.title: Display task progress and hints
clusters.rule: Display task completion status and hints alongside task names to guide user awareness.

clusters.title: Designate one video as main-focus to receive direct playback
clusters.rule: Designate one video as main-focus to receive direct playback controls and audio priority in multiview experiences.

clusters.title: Provide alternate button appearance when button shapes acces
clusters.rule: Provide alternate button appearance when button shapes accessibility setting is enabled.

clusters.title: Use adaptive precision to adjust pointer behavior to match i
clusters.rule: Use adaptive precision to adjust pointer behavior to match interface element size.

clusters.title: Ensure text readability and contrast
clusters.rule: Maintain high contrast ratios between text and background colors for legibility.

clusters.title: Adapt layout to screen size
clusters.rule: Implement responsive layouts that remain usable across different screen sizes with appropriate information prioritization.

clusters.title: Organize space strategically
clusters.rule: Use white space and layout organization strategically to help viewers focus on important information.

clusters.title: Pair metrics with context
clusters.rule: Pair key metrics with context charts showing current, recent, and historical data to help users interpret performance instantly.

clusters.title: Maintain automatic connection stability
clusters.rule: Implement automatic reconnection for WebSocket connections so users do not need to manually refresh dashboards.

clusters.title: Correlate technical metrics
clusters.rule: Include performance correlation displays to help technical teams understand relationships between different metrics.

clusters.title: Centralize analytics for team insight
clusters.rule: Centralize analytics in a single dashboard so teams quickly share insights and accelerate time to market.

findings.finding: 30% more value delivered by data analysts; $3M additional annual revenue by year three

clusters.title: Curate datasets for overview
clusters.rule: Simplify large complex datasets to provide an overview of the most important information at a glance.

clusters.title: Display progress visibly
clusters.rule: Break goals into specific, measurable milestones and display progress visibly to motivate monitoring.

clusters.title: Show device status prominently
clusters.rule: Display device status instantly and prominently on the overview screen without navigation.

clusters.title: Augment styles instead of separate sheets
clusters.rule: Implement dark mode by augmenting existing styles, not loading separate stylesheets.

clusters.title: Prioritize dark mode as built-in feature
clusters.rule: Prioritize dark mode as a built-in feature, not an optional add-on.

clusters.title: Maintain color associations across modes
clusters.rule: Preserve color associations between light and dark modes to maintain visual connection with app icon.

clusters.title: Use adaptive glass materials
clusters.rule: Use glass material for windows so they adapt intelligently to the user's environment lighting.

clusters.title: Use semantic system colors
clusters.rule: Use semantic colors from the system palette instead of hardcoded values to support light and dark modes automatically.

clusters.title: Respect user system preferences
clusters.rule: Respect user system preferences for color scheme, contrast, motion, and font size.

clusters.title: Detect and apply color scheme preference
clusters.rule: Detect user dark mode preference via prefers-color-scheme and apply matching theme to reduce bounce and increase engagement.

findings.finding: 60% reduction in bounce rate and 170% increase in pages per session for dark mode users

clusters.title: Respect user autonomy in theme choice
clusters.rule: Prompt dark-mode users with opt-in rather than forcing theme preference to respect user autonomy.

clusters.title: Maintain high contrast in dark mode
clusters.rule: Ensure high contrast between UI elements and backgrounds, especially in dark mode where the color palette is limited.

clusters.title: Test designs in both light and dark
clusters.rule: Test your interface designs thoroughly in both light and dark modes before release.

clusters.title: Provide user theme toggle option
clusters.rule: Provide users with a toggle option to switch between light and dark modes rather than forcing one mode.

clusters.title: Reduce color saturation in dark mode
clusters.rule: Reduce color saturation in dark mode to prevent colors from appearing too bright or overpowering.

clusters.title: Ensure images and icons visible
clusters.rule: Ensure images and icons remain visible against dark backgrounds by using sufficient contrast.

clusters.title: Offer dark mode for extended use
clusters.rule: Offer dark mode when users spend extended time in your product or use it in varying lighting environments.

clusters.title: Dark mode value is aesthetic contextual
clusters.rule: Dark mode has no measured performance benefit in daytime or well-lit conditions; its value is aesthetic and contextual.

findings.finding: No significant differences in productivity or error rates between dark and light modes in well-lit daytime conditions

clusters.title: Achieve WCAG contrast with desaturated colors
clusters.rule: Achieve WCAG 2 minimum contrast ratio (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text) with desaturated colors on dark backgrounds.

clusters.title: Use font opacity for readability
clusters.rule: Use one font color at varying opacity levels to maintain readability across different dark-mode background colors.

clusters.title: Base spacing on typographic rhythm
clusters.rule: Base vertical spacing on body text line-height to align spacing rhythm with typographic rhythm.

clusters.title: Use CSS custom properties for spacing overrides
clusters.rule: Use CSS custom properties for exception-based spacing overrides within layout contexts.

clusters.title: Space touch targets to prevent accidental selection
clusters.rule: Space touch targets far apart to prevent accidental selection of adjacent controls.

clusters.title: Frame artwork with negative space
clusters.rule: Frame artwork with white negative space so each illustration enhances the app experience and never interrupts it.

clusters.title: Minimum touch target area with size and spacing
clusters.rule: Maintain a minimum target area of 60 points by combining size and spacing for eye-based interaction.

clusters.title: Use 16-point margins for widget alignment
clusters.rule: Use 16-point margins for all widget sizes to maintain consistent spacing with adjacent widgets.

clusters.title: Use 11-point margins for graphical layouts
clusters.rule: Use 11-point margins for layouts with graphical shapes like circles and inset platters to maintain tighter alignment.

clusters.title: Default to compact card spacing
clusters.rule: Use compact spacing (16px) as the default for cards; choose standard (24px) or large (32px) only for specific use cases.

clusters.title: Use consistent padding at all breakpoints
clusters.rule: Use padding of 16 pixels at all standard breakpoints; margins at the outer edge are fixed per breakpoint.

clusters.title: Use small spacing for micro UI components
clusters.rule: Use 0–8px spacing for small UI pieces like icon-text gaps and component padding.

clusters.title: Use spacing to establish visual hierarchy
clusters.rule: Use size and whitespace to establish visual hierarchy and rank elements by importance.

clusters.title: Increase padding between menu options
clusters.rule: Increase padding between menu options to improve selection accuracy, especially on touch devices.

clusters.title: Generous margins in neobrutalist layouts
clusters.rule: Use generous padding of 24–32px margins in neobrutalist layouts to create breathing room and focus attention.

clusters.title: Synchronize shared state in real-time
clusters.rule: Broadcast user changes to the server and all clients immediately to keep shared state current.

clusters.title: Extend branding to browser UI
clusters.rule: Use the theme-color meta tag to align the browser tab bar with your site's design.

clusters.title: Provide discoverable access to hidden controls
clusters.rule: Redisplay hidden UI during immersive experiences using a simple, discoverable gesture.

clusters.title: Minimize checkout distractions
clusters.rule: Remove search bars, app links, category navigation, and tertiary links from checkout flow.

findings.finding: Test #615: 27.6% statistical power at 1% MDE with 206,500 visitors

clusters.title: Clarify ownership in footer
clusters.rule: Include a copyright notice in the footer to clarify who owns the copyright.

clusters.title: Ground decisions in principles
clusters.rule: Base design decisions on universal principles, not techniques, to guide teams consistently.

clusters.title: Make principles memorable and actionable
clusters.rule: Create distinctive, actionable principles that teams remember and use to decide.

clusters.title: Define token foundations before scaling
clusters.rule: Define styling foundations—variables, constants, and shared primitives—before scaling large migrations.

clusters.title: Manage CSS specificity automatically
clusters.rule: Use CSS layers to manage specificity automatically without developer burden.

clusters.title: Establish recognizable product identity
clusters.rule: Configure consistent visual styling across all generated UI results to establish recognizable product identity.

clusters.title: Prevent nested scrolling in cards
clusters.rule: Let cards auto-fit content; prevent nested scrolling that fragments user attention.

clusters.title: Use consistent visual hierarchy
clusters.rule: Apply consistent visual hierarchy across similar components like carousel cards to guide scanning.

clusters.title: Show interaction only when beneficial
clusters.rule: Use cards, carousels, and fullscreen views only when they improve workflow; avoid unnecessary visual complexity.

clusters.title: Separate conversation from execution
clusters.rule: Show conversation and task progress separately with collapsible, auditable execution panels.

clusters.title: Style spacing between elements
clusters.rule: Use adjacent sibling combinators to inject margin between elements, not individual elements.

clusters.title: Use content-aware media queries
clusters.rule: Reconfigure layout based on content requirements, not device type or viewport width.

clusters.title: Enable side-by-side comparison
clusters.rule: Place related options or pricing tiers side-by-side when users must choose between them.

clusters.title: Avoid ad-like styling and placement
clusters.rule: Do not style content to resemble ads or place it near ads; users consciously ignore banner-like information.

clusters.title: Provide signifiers of additional content
clusters.rule: Make it clear when additional content exists so users discover it and expand their options.

clusters.title: Balance consistency with purpose
clusters.rule: Maintain consistency patterns that serve function; remove those that lack purpose and occupy space without value.

clusters.title: Balance simplicity with clarity
clusters.rule: Remove elements strategically while retaining what users need to understand the interface.

clusters.title: De-emphasize navigation and supporting elements
clusters.rule: Make navigation and supporting elements visually recede so main content where users work takes precedence.

clusters.title: Soften structure with rounded separators
clusters.rule: Round separator edges and soften contrast to provide structure without visual clutter.

clusters.title: Maintain consistent grid position
clusters.rule: Use consistent grid position across pages to reduce layout shift perception and show rendering performance.

clusters.title: Use two-column layouts for long-form content
clusters.rule: Organize long-form content into two columns for better navigation and scannability.

clusters.title: Arrange heterogeneous content in one dimension
clusters.rule: Position diverse content in a single dimension with automatic column distribution, not rigid grids.

clusters.title: Let browser compute column layout
clusters.rule: Use auto-fill and minmax() to let the browser compute column count and size instead of forcing fixed layouts.

clusters.title: Use Concentricity APIs for curved displays
clusters.rule: Apply Concentricity APIs to ensure UI fits perfectly in corners on curved displays.

clusters.title: Enlarge UI on larger watch displays
clusters.rule: Scale UI components on Apple Watch Series 7 and later to utilize the expanded content area.

clusters.title: Apply padding only to distortion-prone content
clusters.rule: Use scenePadding modifier selectively on text content that would be distorted or clipped at edges.

clusters.title: Use unified grid-based design
clusters.rule: Apply consistent grid-based design across platforms to maintain visual consistency and support multiple device formats.

clusters.title: Make navigation adaptive and reversible
clusters.rule: Design navigation that resizes without destroying layout and reverts when possible.

clusters.title: Extend content with scroll edge effect
clusters.rule: Extend content around navigation controls using scroll edge effect and space below sidebars.

clusters.title: Use windowed spatial video by default
clusters.rule: Render spatial video with windowed treatment by default; expand immersively only to scale content to real size.

clusters.title: Keep widget snippets under 340 points
clusters.rule: Limit snippet height to under 340 points to avoid scrolling; link to app for additional information.

clusters.title: Use consistent real-world scale for widgets
clusters.rule: Apply real-world proportional scale to widgets so they feel well-positioned in any placement.

clusters.title: Calculate 3D depth in layout systems
clusters.rule: Include depth and Z position alongside width, height, and XY position when laying out 3D views.

clusters.title: Use backgroundExtensionEffect for overlays
clusters.rule: Apply backgroundExtensionEffect to extend content outside safe area without clipping when behind overlays.

clusters.title: Support all watch display dimensions
clusters.rule: Account for all watch display dimensions when designing layouts to deliver same information and actions across screens.

clusters.title: Extend graphics edge-to-edge on watch
clusters.rule: Extend graphic elements and button backgrounds nearly edge-to-edge on watch displays, respecting one-pixel margins.

clusters.title: Use scroll clear areas on watch
clusters.rule: Place scroll clear areas at top and bottom on watch displays to ensure text and buttons are fully visible during scrolling.

clusters.title: Recompile for new watchOS display dimensions
clusters.rule: Recompile watchOS apps to use new display dimensions and create immersive experiences.

clusters.title: Make subscription offers glanceable
clusters.rule: Include value, call to action, login, restore, terms, pricing, and multiple tiers in one glanceable view.

clusters.title: Use layout margins for consistent content alignment
clusters.rule: Apply layout margins to provide consistent content inset and align with controls like navigation bar buttons.

clusters.title: Fill entire display with app content
clusters.rule: Extend app content to fill the entire display; avoid black bars at top or bottom that make apps feel small.

clusters.title: Consider device aspect ratios for backgrounds
clusters.rule: Design background graphics for various aspect ratios across devices to maintain visual integrity.

clusters.title: Present momentary information on top
clusters.rule: Place alerts, sheets, menus, and popovers on top of volumes so they break through content and stay visible.

clusters.title: Configure dynamic bounds for AR blending
clusters.rule: Set dynamic bounds restrictions to allow app content to peek beyond bounds and blend with the real world.

clusters.title: Position tab bars at app top
clusters.rule: Place tab bars at the top of the app near navigation controls to make them easier to reach.

clusters.title: Enable multiview layout templates
clusters.rule: Support multiview layout templates that maximize comfort and ergonomics for multiple simultaneous video screens.

clusters.title: Keep interactive elements at same depth
clusters.rule: Maintain all interactive content at the same depth to avoid eye strain from refocusing.

clusters.title: Use translucent materials for hierarchy
clusters.rule: Apply translucent materials to establish hierarchy and clarify navigation context within the system.

clusters.title: Prioritize visibility through sizing
clusters.rule: Make information and elements visible at a quick glance through appropriate sizing and scaling.

clusters.title: Integrate logo marks into structure
clusters.rule: Integrate logo marks into layout structure rather than displaying the full app icon.

clusters.title: Dynamically adjust Live Activity height
clusters.rule: Adjust Live Activity height based on available information to reduce clutter.

clusters.title: Present shared activities in windowed view
clusters.rule: Show shared activities in windowed treatment to support multitasking and collaboration without leaving surroundings.

clusters.title: Avoid launching unrelated windows
clusters.rule: Do not launch extra windows unrelated to the shared activity.

clusters.title: Center app icon graphics
clusters.rule: Keep app icon graphics centered to avoid appearing off-center when expanded.

clusters.title: Make headers and buttons prominent
clusters.rule: Design headers and buttons to stand out since people do not read screens linearly.

clusters.title: Place share button in toolbars
clusters.rule: Position the share button in toolbars where users can easily access it.

clusters.title: Remove abstraction layers for direct interaction
clusters.rule: Let users interact directly with physical surroundings via device proximity instead of through abstraction layers.

clusters.title: Keep watchOS apps lightweight and glanceable
clusters.rule: Limit watchOS app interactions and display essential information at a glance without scrolling.

clusters.title: Place Add to Siri buttons selectively
clusters.rule: Position Add to Siri buttons near high-intent actions only, not on every menu item.

clusters.title: Support Auto Layout for iPad to Mac
clusters.rule: Implement Auto Layout fully so iPad app layouts adapt to arbitrary Mac window resizing.

clusters.title: Remove nonessential UI elements
clusters.rule: Strip away UI elements that do not serve the immediate task so people focus on essential actions.

clusters.title: Place controls in consistent locations
clusters.rule: Position controls in consistent, predictable locations throughout your interface to improve usability.

clusters.title: Build hierarchy with order, spacing, contrast
clusters.rule: Use order, spacing, and contrast to guide attention to the most important item on screen.

clusters.title: Create unexpectedness through context breaks
clusters.rule: Break context by placing dissimilar elements among similar ones to make them memorable.

clusters.title: Place primary search in bottom toolbar
clusters.rule: Position primary search in iOS bottom toolbar for ergonomic reachability; field animates up over keyboard.

clusters.title: Offset content from folding edge
clusters.rule: Move content away from the right edge when controls occupy vertical space on folds.

clusters.title: Use displacement patterns preserving relationships
clusters.rule: Apply displacement patterns to move elements away from the fold while preserving relationships and meaning.

clusters.title: Override alignment guides semantically
clusters.rule: Use semantic alignment guide overrides to position views without manual offset calculations.

clusters.title: Viewers see 81° of immersive content
clusters.rule: Compose immersive visionOS scenes within approximately 81° of viewer's field of view.

findings.finding: 81 degrees field of view

clusters.title: Prevent overlapping glass elements
clusters.rule: Keep glass elements from overlapping to maintain the illusion of a single floating control layer.

clusters.title: Customize 3D view depth alignment
clusters.rule: Set custom depth alignment (front, center, back) on Layout types to position 3D views properly.

clusters.title: Use SpatialContainer for 3D alignment
clusters.rule: Apply SpatialContainer to align multiple 3D views in the same space with 3D alignment guides.

clusters.title: Use spatialOverlay for 3D view overlay
clusters.rule: Apply spatialOverlay to overlay a single 3D view in the same space as another with 3D alignment.

clusters.title: Maintain consistent field-of-view coverage
clusters.rule: Use dynamic scaling so UI maintains the same field-of-view coverage regardless of window distance.

clusters.title: Limit watchOS page to single screen height
clusters.rule: Restrict each watchOS page to single screen height to encourage focused purpose and glanceability.

clusters.title: Arrange important toolbar items trailing
clusters.rule: Position important toolbar items in trailing section to remain visible across window size changes.

clusters.title: Group related toolbar actions together
clusters.rule: Organize related toolbar actions together to keep them grouped and prevent toolbar overflow.

clusters.title: Reduce Live Activity height dynamically
clusters.rule: Decrease Live Activity height when information decreases to minimize lock screen space used.

clusters.title: Make Dynamic Island Compact view narrow
clusters.rule: Keep Dynamic Island Compact view as narrow as possible with content snug against the sensor region.

clusters.title: Maintain relative element placement in Dynamic Island
clusters.rule: Keep relative placement consistent between Dynamic Island Compact and Expanded views for coherence.

clusters.title: Allow separate personal windows with shared context
clusters.rule: Enable individuals to open separate personal windows while maintaining shared context for group coordination.

clusters.title: Use screen space overlay for AR text
clusters.rule: Place text and buttons in screen space overlay rather than in 3D world to preserve legibility in AR.

clusters.title: Position collaboration button prominently
clusters.rule: Place the collaboration button next to the share button where it stands out as a primary feature.

clusters.title: Keep collaboration popover glanceable
clusters.rule: Keep collaboration popover middle section concise and glanceable; avoid overloading with info or buttons.

clusters.title: Position instructions where users look
clusters.rule: Place on-screen instructions where users are already looking, not in arbitrary locations.

clusters.title: Size interactive elements for touch targets
clusters.rule: Keep interactive elements centered with at least 60 points of tap target area and 8 points minimum spacing.

findings.finding: 60 points minimum tap target; 44-point button requires 8 points spacing

clusters.title: Overlap ornaments into window edges
clusters.rule: Position ornaments overlapping the bottom edge by 20 points to integrate visually with the main window.

findings.finding: 20-point overlap for bottom-edge ornaments

clusters.title: Keep UI in viewer's field of view
clusters.rule: Position all UI within people's field of view, avoiding locations too high, low, or far that require head rotation.

clusters.title: Use wider aspect ratios with horizontal extension
clusters.rule: Design with wider aspect ratios and horizontal canvas extension rather than vertical for ergonomic head movement.

clusters.title: Use opaque circular achievement images
clusters.rule: Display achievement images as opaque circles centered; system automatically crops to circle shape.

clusters.title: Size menu items smaller than action sheets
clusters.rule: Make menu items smaller and more concise than action sheet items while keeping them easily tappable.

clusters.title: Match pointer precision to interface
clusters.rule: Reduce pointer precision for low-precision controls like buttons; increase for high-precision interfaces.

clusters.title: Use center alignment for symbols
clusters.rule: Center-align symbols rather than using aspect fit or scale to fit to maintain optical balance.

clusters.title: Remove nonessential UI for approximate location
clusters.rule: Strip UI requiring precise location data when users share only approximate location instead.

clusters.title: Use CSS environment variables for safe areas
clusters.rule: Apply CSS environment variables to dynamically position content clear of notches and tab bars.

clusters.title: Use viewport-fit=cover for edge extension
clusters.rule: Apply viewport-fit=cover in meta viewport to extend content to edges; use environment variables for safe areas.

clusters.title: Use Flexbox or Grid for tab bar interaction
clusters.rule: Apply Flexbox or CSS Grid so content hugs expanding tab bar; content above stays fixed.

clusters.title: Place action buttons at detail view bottom
clusters.rule: Position action buttons at the bottom of detail views, applying only to content above them.

clusters.title: Deliver carousel images at full screen
clusters.rule: Provide carousel images at 1920 by 1080 points filling the entire frame for full-screen display.

clusters.title: Show navigation alongside iPad content
clusters.rule: Keep navigation visible alongside content simultaneously on iPad instead of in overlays or modals.

clusters.title: Avoid modal overlays on iPad
clusters.rule: Keep controls at the same level as content on iPad so users see results and context simultaneously.

clusters.title: Move iPad bottom edge controls to Mac toolbar
clusters.rule: Relocate iPad bottom edge controls to Mac toolbar to prevent hiding below the dock.

clusters.title: Sort items by filter matching
clusters.rule: Arrange items higher on page when they satisfy more filters if otherwise unsorted.

clusters.title: Arrange elements along continuing lines
clusters.rule: Position elements along smooth, continuing lines rather than ragged ones to show they belong together.

clusters.title: Group filters close to controlled content
clusters.rule: Place filters and navigation elements close together; position view-specific filters near the views they control.

clusters.title: Center images in small tiles
clusters.rule: Use centered images in small tiles to draw attention; left-align text and actions as a block.

clusters.title: Use one primary button per empty state
clusters.rule: Show one primary button per empty state context to emphasize the main action.

clusters.title: Hide unnecessary empty state UI
clusters.rule: Hide unnecessary UI elements in blank content empty states unless content is hidden but accessible.

clusters.title: Match skeleton to content dimensions
clusters.rule: Build skeleton loaders with dimensions exactly matching content layout to prevent layout shifts.

clusters.title: Use ContextView as default entry point
clusters.rule: Build app views with a ContextView as the default entry point to display content alongside Stripe pages.

clusters.title: Position information elements nearby content
clusters.rule: Place titles near charts, legends close to charts they serve, and filters adjacent to charts they influence.

clusters.title: Align perceptual and interaction objects
clusters.rule: Ensure elements that look selectable as one unit respond together; perceptual and interaction objects must align.

clusters.title: Reserve whitespace to separate chunks
clusters.rule: Use whitespace to separate visual chunks; dense layouts trigger grouping collapse where all elements cluster.

clusters.title: Use proportional grid division
clusters.rule: Divide space by two to create fluid grids; multiply fixed units by two to create fixed grids.

clusters.title: Scale grid by column or box size
clusters.rule: Scale column count by tiling fixed boxes if users want more items; scale box size with fixed columns for more content per item.

clusters.title: Use primary buttons only once per screen
clusters.rule: Reserve primary button styling for the principal call to action; do not repeat on the same screen.

clusters.title: Do not mix button sizes in groups
clusters.rule: Keep all button sizes consistent within button groups.

clusters.title: Avoid multiple high-emphasis buttons
clusters.rule: Do not use two high-emphasis buttons in a button group.

clusters.title: Align checkbox text below at top
clusters.rule: Position wrapped text beneath checkboxes aligned at the top, never vertically centered with the checkbox.

clusters.title: Keep modal content inset from edges
clusters.rule: Never place labels or text in modal margins; only full-width components like tables may extend to edges.

clusters.title: Align dropdown containers to grid columns
clusters.rule: Position default-style dropdown containers flush to grid columns so labels align with other page elements.

clusters.title: Organize layouts linearly
clusters.rule: Arrange layouts linearly to minimize friction since humans parse shapes sequentially, not in parallel.
